title: Ice Soldiers
tagline: The Cold War Begins Again.
overview: A scientist discovers the bodies of three frozen genetically modified Russians buried in the Canadian North. Upon thawing them out he realizes he has unleashed a deadly threat to Western society and must stop them at all costs.
plot:
Ice Soldiers is a 2013 Canadian action science fiction film directed by Sturla Gunnarsson. Dominic Purcell stars as scientist Andrew Malraux, with Adam Beach as T.C. Cardinal, Michael Ironside as Colonel Desmond Trump and Gabriel Hogan as the leader of three frozen Soviet super soldiers.

The film opens in 1962, during the Cuban Missile Crisis, when Canadian troops in the Arctic find a crashed aircraft carrying three Soviet soldiers with superhuman abilities. Taken to a base for study, they break free, kill many troops and vanish. Fifty years later, a team of Canadian soldiers and scientists, including Malraux and Dr. Lobokoff, finds the three soldiers frozen beneath the ice. Malraux explains that Soviet extremists, aided by a captured Nazi scientist, engineered them to attack New York and trigger a third world war. The bodies prove to be alive and regenerating. When the team cannot agree on what to do, Malraux tries to kill them by cutting off their life support and is locked up. His fears prove justified: the soldiers wake up and massacre most of the team, including Lobokoff.

Malraux escapes and pursues them across the frozen landscape with T.C., a troubled Cree ex-convict whose father survived the soldiers' first rampage in the 1960s. They track the soldiers to a small oil town, where the three have learned of a mine where they can steal explosives. Arriving too late, Malraux and T.C. are wrongly arrested for the theft and the murder of the miners. No one heeds Malraux's warning about the soldiers' preprogrammed mission. That night, the soldiers blow up the power plant and kill local officials and police. Malraux and T.C. escape and chase the soldiers' truck by snowmobile, tricking it into crashing into a mountainside. The explosion kills two of the soldiers. The third heads for a plane bound for New York, and Malraux drags him off and kills him after a brutal fight. As they cremate the body, Malraux reveals that his mother was a scientist who examined the soldiers in the 1960s and was raped by this man, making him the soldier's son. T.C. assures him that he is a good man, but Malraux remains unsure.

The film was shot in 2013 around Sudbury, Ontario. Gunnarsson, staging storms with wind machines and a snowmobile chase, called it a "big toybox". It premiered in Sudbury on February 28, 2014. Critics dismissed it as generic B-movie fare, and Canada.com called it a gleefully preposterous slice of B-movie cheese.

title: Barbie: The Pearl Princess

overview: Barbie plays Lumina, a mermaid girl with the power to change the color of pearls. Cheerful and creative, Lumina finds herself working in a mermaid salon customizing fabulous hairstyles. And when Lumina has the chance to attend the royal ball, her friends adorn her with a gown fit for a princess. At the ball, villains try to seize power over the kingdom, and Lumina finds within herself an unexpected power that proves she is much more than a hair stylist.
plot:
Barbie: The Pearl Princess is a 2014 American-Canadian computer-animated fantasy film and the 27th entry in the Barbie film series. Directed by Zeke Norton from a screenplay by Cydne Clark and Steve Granat, it was produced by Barbie Entertainment with animation by Rainmaker Entertainment, featured music by Jim Dooley, and was released direct to home video by Universal, appearing in France in February 2014 and in the United States on 11 March 2014. It runs 73 minutes and includes the songs "Mermaid Party" and "Light Up the World".

Kelly Sheridan voices Lumina, a cheerful seventeen-year-old mermaid who can make pearls glow and move at her command. She lives on a remote reef with her seahorse friend Kuda (Katie Crown) and her stern aunt Scylla (Trish Pattendon), who forbids her to show her power. In the royal capital, King Nereus and Queen Lorelei still mourn a daughter lost years earlier, and the king's brother-in-law Caligo (John Novak) arranges a royal ball at which his son Fergis, heir in the absence of the princess, is to find a wife. Caligo secretly sends his eel henchman Murray to force Scylla, a potion-maker, to poison the king at the ball.

Finding the invitation Scylla left behind, Lumina sets off for the city with Kuda, befriending a lonely spiny fish named Spike along the way. There she becomes a celebrated hairstylist at the salon of the octopus Madame Ruckus, using her pearls to create dazzling styles, meets the visiting Prince Delphin, and watches the gentle Fergis, who would rather be a botanist, fall for her co-worker Cora. Caligo, meanwhile, realises from a hidden royal bracelet that Lumina is the missing princess and has her imprisoned, but she escapes using her powers.

At the ball Lumina knocks the poisoned cup from the king's hand. When Scylla tries to reveal the plot, Caligo pushes her onto one of Spike's venomous spines, and she confesses that she took Lumina away as a baby on Caligo's orders but chose to raise her instead of harming her. Fergis supplies a rare lily that cures her, and Lumina uses her pearls to stop Caligo. The queen reveals that she shares the same pearl magic, a royal gift, confirming Lumina's identity; the princess is reunited with her parents and asks that Scylla and Kuda join her at the palace.

The voice cast also includes Mark Oliver as Nereus, Rebecca Shoichet as Lorelei, Simon Hill as Fergis, Peter New as Murray and Kathleen Barr as Madame Ruckus.

As the story progresses, it becomes clear that there are supernatural forces at play. The film features stunning visuals and action sequences, showcasing the epic battles between good and evil.

One of the most significant plot twists in the film is the revelation about Mahendra's past. It is revealed that he was once a prince who was next in line to the throne but was forced to flee after his half-brother Bhallaladeva took over as the rightful heir. This sets off a chain of events that leads to the final confrontation between the two brothers.

The film culminates in an epic battle between Mahendra and Bhallaladeva, with the fate of the kingdom hanging in the balance. In the end, it is revealed that Bhallaladeva was actually the rightful king all along, and he defeats his half-brother to reclaim his throne.

Overall, Bāhubali: The Beginning is an epic fantasy adventure film that features stunning visuals, action sequences, and a complex plot. While the ending may be divisive, the film's themes of loyalty, duty, and redemption are timeless and universal.

title: As Above, So Below
tagline: The only way out is down
overview: When a team of explorers ventures into the catacombs that lie beneath the streets of Paris, they uncover the dark secret that lies within this city of the dead.
plot:
As Above, So Below is a 2014 American found-footage horror film directed by John Erick Dowdle and written by Dowdle and Drew Dowdle. The movie follows a group of explorers who venture into the Paris catacombs in search of a mythical treasure.

The story begins with a prologue that sets the tone for the rest of the film. A young girl, named Sarah (played by Perdita Weeks), is shown to be obsessed with the idea of finding the Philosopher's Stone, a legendary alchemical substance believed to have the power to transform base metals into gold and grant eternal life.

The main characters, including Sarah, her boyfriend Dylan (played by Ben Feldman), and their friends Anthony (played by Edwin Hodge) and Jean (played by Pierre Piffaretti), are all part of an urban exploration group. They decide to explore the Paris catacombs in search of a mythical treasure that is said to be hidden deep within the tunnels.

As they venture deeper into the catacombs, the group begins to experience strange occurrences and supernatural events. They soon realize that they are not alone in the tunnels, and that the catacombs hold many dark secrets and terrors.

Throughout the film, the group's dynamics and relationships begin to fray as tensions rise and the group becomes increasingly paranoid. The tension builds up as they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, narrow passageways, and terrifying creatures.

As the group delves deeper into the catacombs, they stumble upon an ancient ritual that is said to have been performed by a secret society of alchemists. They soon realize that they are being led deeper into the tunnels by some unknown force, which seems to be manipulating their actions.

The film's climax features a series of intense and terrifying events as the group faces off against a monstrous creature that has been awakened by their presence in the catacombs. In the end, only one member of the group manages to escape the catacombs alive, but not without being forever changed by her experience.

Throughout the film, the title "As Above, So Below" is referenced as a phrase from an ancient alchemical text that suggests that the macrocosm (the universe) and the microcosm (humanity) are connected. The film's use of this phrase serves as a metaphor for the idea that our actions have consequences, both in the physical world and in the spiritual realm.

Overall, As Above, So Below is a tense and terrifying horror film that explores themes of obsession, paranoia, and the supernatural. With its claustrophobic setting and creepy atmosphere, the film is sure to appeal to fans of the horror genre.

title: In the Blood
tagline: She Will Stop At Nothing
overview: When her husband goes missing during their Caribbean vacation, a woman sets off on her own to take down the men she thinks are responsible.
plot:
In the Blood is a 2014 American action thriller directed by John Stockwell. Gina Carano, the former mixed martial artist, stars in her second leading role after Haywire (2011) as Ava, a newlywed searching for her missing husband, with Cam Gigandet as her husband Derek, Luis Guzmán, Stephen Lang, Danny Trejo, Amaury Nolasco and Treat Williams. It was released in April 2014.

In 2002, fourteen-year-old Ava wakes in the night to see her father, a drug lord, murdered by intruders, and she kills the attackers with a shotgun. Twelve years later, after a troubled life and recovery from drug and alcohol addiction, she marries Derek Grant, a wealthy man she met at Narcotics Anonymous. The couple honeymoon on a Caribbean island where Derek's family owns a vacation home. They befriend a young local, Manny, who invites them to a nightclub, where, after an encounter with a local criminal known as Big Biz, Ava fights off several patrons.

The next morning, Manny takes them to ride a long zip line through the rainforest. Ava, who is afraid of heights, refuses, but Derek goes ahead; his harness snaps and he falls into the trees. Ava finds him unconscious but alive. Forbidden to ride in the ambulance, she follows to the hospital, but the staff insist that Derek was never brought in, and no other clinic on the island has any record of him. She reports him missing, but the local police, led by a skeptical chief, suspect that Ava herself may be responsible. Derek's father arrives and also blames her. Using the fighting skills taught to her by her father, Ava begins her own investigation, confronting the zip-line operators, Big Biz and other members of the island's criminal underworld, and uncovering the truth behind the staged accident, as she fights her way toward the people who kidnapped her husband.

In the Blood received mixed reviews, with a 38 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Ben Kenigsberg of Variety called it a serviceable action vehicle, while Nick Schager of The Village Voice found it grim and formulaic but praised Carano's charm, and Andy Webster of The New York Times also commended her.

The movie's climax features an intense and action-packed sequence as Nicky and Jess face off against their rivals in a thrilling game of cat and mouse. In the end, they emerge victorious, but not without some unexpected twists and turns.

One of the most interesting aspects of Focus is its exploration of the complex relationship between Nicky and Jess. Will Smith brings his signature charm and charisma to the role of Nicky, while Margot Robbie shines as the feisty and talented Jess.

Overall, Focus is a fun and entertaining movie that combines witty banter, clever plot twists, and plenty of action. With its strong performances and engaging storyline, it's no wonder that this movie was a commercial success and helped establish Will Smith and Margot Robbie as two of Hollywood's most exciting young stars.

title: Toy Story That Time Forgot

overview: During a post-Christmas play date, the gang find themselves in uncharted territory when the coolest set of action figures ever turn out to be dangerously delusional. It's all up to Trixie, the triceratops, if the gang hopes to return to Bonnie's room in this Toy Story That Time Forgot.
plot:
Toy Story That Time Forgot is an American animated Christmas television special produced by Pixar Animation Studios and Disney Television Animation, written and directed by Steve Purcell. It aired on ABC on December 2, 2014. Set after the Toy Story Toons shorts and months before Toy Story 4, it brings back Tom Hanks, Tim Allen, Kristen Schaal, Wallace Shawn, Timothy Dalton, Don Rickles and Joan Cusack, with Kevin McKidd and Emma Hudak voicing new characters and music by Michael Giacchino. It was Rickles's last television special role before his death in 2017.

Trixie, a toy triceratops, is frustrated that Bonnie never casts her as a dinosaur in playtime. On December 27, Bonnie brings Trixie, Woody, Buzz Lightyear, Rex and Angel Kitty, a Christmas ornament given to spouting holiday morals, to a play date at her cousin Mason's house. Instead of playing with them, Bonnie tosses the toys into Mason's playroom and joins him at his new video game console. The playroom is dominated by Mason's new Battlesaurs playset, a tribe of armored dinosaur warriors led by the gallant Reptillus Maximus and a pteranodon-like shaman called the Cleric. Delighted to be treated as a dinosaur at last, Trixie is armed as a warrior alongside Rex and grows close to Reptillus, unaware that Woody and Buzz have been taken prisoner.

Trixie soon learns that the Battlesaurs have never been played with and do not realize they are toys. When Mason's other toys are attacked in a gladiatorial arena and Woody and Buzz are forced to fight, Trixie defends them, and the Cleric brands her a heretic because Bonnie's name is written on her foot. She flees to fetch Bonnie, and Reptillus, sent after her, is enraged to see his own toy packaging. Meanwhile the Cleric, who knows the truth and has exploited Mason's neglect to rule the playroom, takes control of Rex's robotic weapons and plans to dump Woody, Buzz and Angel Kitty down an air vent. In Mason's bedroom, Trixie explains the meaning of playtime, and Reptillus reluctantly switches off the game. The children rediscover the toys, return to the playroom in time to save Woody and Buzz, and play happily with everyone. Back home, Trixie proudly calls herself Bonnie's dinosaur, content with any role Bonnie gives her.

The special drew 6.79 million viewers on ABC and was acclaimed by critics, earning 92% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 81.

title: Danny Collins
tagline: A letter from John Lennon changed his life
overview: An ageing hard-living 1970s rock star decides to change his life when he discovers a 40-year-old undelivered letter written to him by John Lennon.
plot:
Aging 1970s rocker Danny Collins cannot give up his hard-living ways, but his manager Frank Grubman uncovers a 40-year-old undelivered letter to him from John Lennon. After reading the letter, Danny decides to change his way of life. He travels to New Jersey to attempt to connect for the first time with his grown son, Tom Donnelly, born from a casual relationship with a woman who died 10 years earlier. Tom has a wife, Samantha, and seven-year-old daughter Hope, and is expecting a second child.
Seeking a new start, Danny forswears touring and checks into a Hilton hotel in New Jersey, much to the delight of the young staff. He begins to woo the hotel manager Mary, and tries to set up her assistant Jamie on a date.
Tom initially rejects the father who he believes abandoned him, but Danny persists, arranging for Hope, who has ADHD, to be accepted into an exclusive school for children with special needs. plot:

However, his life is turned upside down when he receives an invitation from the President of the United States (played by Keegan-Michael Key) to attend a high-stakes meeting at the White House.

Paul travels to Washington D.C. with his new partner, Amy (Jayma Mays), a tough and no-nonsense Secret Service agent. As they navigate the city, they encounter various obstacles and challenges, including Simon's henchmen and a series of hilarious mishaps.

As Paul delves deeper into the plot, he discovers that Simon has a personal vendetta against him and is determined to ruin his reputation as a mall cop. The two engage in an epic battle, with Paul using his wits and his security skills to outsmart Simon's henchmen and ultimately foil his plans.

Throughout the movie, Kevin James delivers his signature blend of humor and heart, bringing Paul Blart to life once again. The film also features a talented supporting cast, including Keegan-Michael Key, Jayma Mays, and Neal Brennan.

The ending of the movie sees Paul successfully stopping Simon and saving the day. However, in a surprising twist, it is revealed that Simon was actually working for a larger conspiracy involving corrupt government officials. The movie ends with Paul returning to his life as a mall cop, but with a newfound sense of purpose and a deeper understanding of the importance of his work.

Overall, Paul Blart: Mall Cop 2 is a lighthearted and entertaining film that delivers on its promise of action, comedy, and adventure. While it may not be as memorable as its predecessor, it remains a fun and enjoyable ride for fans of Kevin James and the Paul Blart franchise.

title: Little Boy
tagline: Believe the impossible.
overview: An eight-year-old boy is willing to do whatever it takes to end World War II so he can bring his father home. The story reveals the indescribable love a father has for his little boy and the love a son has for his father.
plot:
In the seaside town of O'Hare, California, an 8-year-old boy who is small for his age, Pepper Flynt Busbee, has a very close relationship with James, his loving father, which begins from the very moment he is born when his father cradles him in his arms and notices how small he is. When Pepper asks a doctor if he has dwarfism, the doctor tells him, "For now, Pepper, let's just say you're a 'little boy.'" This expression becomes Pepper's nickname. He comes to despise those two words and always makes a problem when someone calls him by his nickname.
However, when World War II begins, Pepper's older brother is declared ineligible for military service because of flat feet and their father joins in his place, which devastates Pepper. Not long after his father leaves for war, Pepper hears the Bible verse, "Truly I tell you, if you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move" (Matthew 17:20), and he becomes determined to get enough faith to bring his father home. Nevertheless, as his friend and mentor Father Oliver tells him, faith is useless to anyone who harbors hatred. Father Oliver tells Pepper to befriend a Japanese man named Hashimoto.
At first, the anti-Japanese sentiment Pepper has internalized – which has become prevalent in his society – makes him hesitant to follow this advice, but as he gets to know Hashimoto, he begins to value their friendship and learns from Hashimoto to stand up to those who bully him about his height. Father Oliver gives Pepper a list of tasks to complete. When Pepper's father is reported missing in action, Pepper's mother struggles to keep her family together in the face of these overwhelming hardships. His brother London, and Sam – one of the townspeople who lost a son – go to Hashimoto's home and attack him one night, leading to his being hospitalized. London is initially arrested, but Hashimoto decides not to press charges, so London is released.
An Army representative brings the news that Pepper's father has been killed and is buried in the Philippines. Hashimoto goes to the memorial service at the O'Hare Cemetery to pay his respects. Pepper and Hashimoto sit on a bench and discuss their mutual losses of family and belief. Pepper goes back to the cemetery to visit his father's grave and place the list on top of his grave marker. Pepper and his mother visit the town doctor, Dr. Fox, who flirts with Pepper’s mom and invites himself over that evening, claiming he wants to discuss the cause of Pepper’s short stature.
Later that day, a spokesperson from the Army arrives to tell Pepper's mom that James didn't die after all. The man who died had been wearing James’ boots, with his dog tags attached, and was mistakenly identified as James after being shot. The family leaves town to visit James in the hospital, and Pepper gifts James the boots that he had coveted for some time. When they arrive, they realize that James has mild amnesia from a head injury.

title: Point Break
tagline: The only law that matters is gravity
overview: A young undercover FBI agent infiltrates a gang of thieves who share a common interest in extreme sports. A remake of the 1991 film, "Point Break".
plot:
Point Break is a 2015 action thriller directed and shot by Ericson Core and written by Kurt Wimmer, a remake of the 1991 film of the same name that starred Patrick Swayze and Keanu Reeves. An American, German and Chinese co-production, it stars Luke Bracey as Johnny Utah, a former extreme athlete turned FBI recruit, Édgar Ramírez as Bodhi, the charismatic leader of a group of thrill-seeking criminals, Teresa Palmer as Samsara, Ray Winstone as FBI agent Angelo Pappas and Delroy Lindo.

Utah, a motocross star, gives up extreme sports after his best friend dies during a stunt. Seven years later, as a candidate to become an FBI agent, he studies a series of spectacular crimes, including a diamond heist from a skyscraper in Mumbai with an escape by parachute and a raid in Mexico in which stolen cash is scattered over the countryside. He concludes that the robberies were carried out by the same team, which is attempting to complete the Ozaki 8, a series of eight extreme ordeals meant to honor the forces of nature.

Predicting that the group will attempt the next ordeal on a giant wave in France, Utah goes undercover with Pappas. After nearly drowning, he is rescued by Bodhi and welcomed into his circle, where he meets Samsara and is drawn into a world of daring feats, including wingsuit flying through Alpine cliffs and extreme snowboarding down a steep mountain. As Utah grows closer to the group and begins to share their philosophy, he becomes torn between loyalty to his new friends and his duty as an agent, while the gang's actions grow increasingly dangerous and deadly. Utah must ultimately stop Bodhi before the final ordeal.

The film puts its emphasis on real extreme sports stunts shot in locations around the world, presenting the robberies as acts of eco-activism.

Released in China on December 4, 2015, and in the United States on December 25 by Warner Bros., Point Break grossed about 134 million dollars against a 105 million dollar budget. Critics considered it inferior to the original, giving it 11 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 34.

The movie follows Ben Whittaker (played by Robert De Niro), a retired executive who decides to pursue his long-held passion for gardening. He moves to New York City and applies for an internship at a fashion startup called Second Act, founded by Jules Ostin (played by Anne Hathaway). As the story unfolds, Ben and Jules grow closer, and their friendship deepens. They share stories about their past, support each other through tough times, and learn from each other's experiences. Through their bond, they find common ground and discover that age is just a number.

The film explores themes of friendship, mentorship, and the importance of human connection in a rapidly changing world. It highlights the value of intergenerational relationships and challenges societal norms around work, aging, and identity.

Ultimately, The Intern is a heartwarming story about finding purpose, belonging, and happiness at any age. Ben and Jules's unlikely friendship becomes a source of inspiration for those around them, reminding us that it's never too late to pursue our passions and make a positive impact on the world.

title: Pixels

overview: Video game experts are recruited by the military to fight 1980s-era video game characters who've attacked New York.
plot:
Pixels is a 2015 science fiction comedy film directed by Chris Columbus and produced by Columbia Pictures. The movie takes place in modern-day New York City, where alien invasions are a common occurrence.

The story begins with a group of gamers who compete in an online video game called "Pixelon," which allows players to control digital avatars and battle each other. Among the gamers is Eddie Plant (Adam Sandler), a 39-year-old man-child who still lives with his mother, Carol (Brenda Strong). Eddie's life takes a dramatic turn when he receives a message from his childhood friend, Owen (Peter Dinklage), who has been recruited by the government to help defend the Earth against an alien invasion.

The aliens, known as the "Pac-Landians," are from the classic arcade game Pac-Man and have come to Earth to destroy it. The Pac-Landians are led by Balthazar (Kevin James), a giant, mutated version of Pac-Man who is determined to eat all the humans on the planet.

Eddie, Owen, and their friends, including Sam (Josh Gad) and Margo (Kelly Overton), must use their gaming skills to defeat the aliens and save humanity. Along the way, Eddie also reunites with his high school sweetheart, Sarah (Ashley Judd), who is now a scientist working for the government.

As the battle between humans and Pac-Landians intensifies, Eddie and his friends discover that they have the ability to control digital avatars from classic arcade games, such as Donkey Kong, Galaga, and Centipede. They use these avatars to fight back against the aliens and eventually defeat Balthazar.

The movie features a mix of action, comedy, and nostalgia for classic video games. The special effects are impressive, with the digital avatars coming to life in a way that is both entertaining and believable. The cast delivers solid performances, with Adam Sandler bringing his signature humor and charm to the lead role.

Overall, Pixels is a fun and lighthearted movie that is sure to appeal to fans of science fiction, comedy, and classic video games. While it may not be a masterpiece of storytelling, it is an enjoyable ride that is full of action, adventure, and nostalgia for the 1980s.

title: The Darkness
tagline: Evil comes home
overview: A family returns from a Grand Canyon vacation with a supernatural presence in tow.
plot:
The Darkness is an American supernatural horror film of 2016 directed by Greg McLean, who co-wrote it with Shayne Armstrong and Shane Krause, about a family that brings home a malevolent force from the Grand Canyon. Kevin Bacon and Radha Mitchell play Peter and Bronny Taylor, with David Mazouz as their autistic son Mikey, Lucy Fry as their daughter Stephanie, and Matt Walsh and Jennifer Morrison as their friends the Carters.

On a holiday at the Grand Canyon in Arizona with another family, the Carters, Mikey wanders into a small cave and finds black stones carved with symbols, which he takes home. Soon strange things begin to happen in the Taylors' house: the kitchen taps keep turning on, and handprints appear on a mirror, incidents Mikey blames on someone he calls "Jenny". Stephanie, who has been secretly bulimic, is caught hiding vomit under her bed, and her parents take her for treatment, leaving Mikey with Bronny's mother, who catches him trying to kill her cat.

Searching online, Bronny learns that the Anasazi believed demons were bound to stones hidden in caves; if the stones are removed, the spirits take the forms of a crow, a snake, a coyote, a wolf and a buffalo, attach themselves to young children and draw them into their world in an event called the Darkness. The only way to banish the demons is for someone without fear to return the stones to where they were found. The haunting intensifies: after a fire in his room, Mikey is found soot-marked and bleeding from the mouth; Bronny, plagued by nightmares of a wolf, starts drinking; and invisible hands choke Stephanie until Peter, who has seen a coyote and a shadowy figure, rushes in. The burned patch of Mikey's wall turns out to be a portal.

Peter calls a healer named Teresa, recommended by his boss, who arrives with her granddaughter Gloria as interpreter. As they cleanse the house, they find that the true evil resides in Mikey's room and begin a chant while the boy walks into the portal with the demons. Peter follows with the stones but is too afraid to set them down and offers to take his son's place. Mikey, who is not afraid, puts the stones down himself, ending the Darkness, and father and son leap back out before the portal vanishes and Gloria declares the house cleansed.

Filmed in Los Angeles in April and May 2014, the film was released on Friday 13 May 2016 by Blumhouse Tilt and High Top Releasing. It was panned by critics but earned $10.9 million on a $4 million budget.

The Punisher grapples with his own sense of justice and the consequences of his actions, while Black Widow struggles with her loyalty to S.H.I.E.L.D. and her growing feelings for a mysterious ally.

As the stakes escalate, the duo discovers that HYDRA's plan involves using advanced technology to create an army of super-soldiers, which they intend to use to take over the world. The Punisher and Black Widow must put aside their differences and work together to stop HYDRA's sinister plans.

The film culminates in a thrilling showdown between the heroes and HYDRA's forces, with the Punisher and Black Widow facing off against the Red Wolf in an intense battle. In the end, they succeed in defeating HYDRA and destroying its plans for world domination.

Overall, Avengers Confidential: Black Widow & Punisher is an entertaining and action-packed take on two beloved Marvel characters, offering a fresh perspective on their respective stories while maintaining the spirit of the larger MCU.

title: Term Life
tagline: A daughter out of options. A father out of time.
overview: If Nick Barrow can stay alive for 21 days, he'll die happy. Everyone Nick knows wants him dead; Mob bosses, contract killers, and dirty cops. plot:
Term Life is a 2016 American action drama directed by Peter Billingsley from a screenplay by A. J. Lieberman, based on Lieberman's graphic novel of the same name. It stars Vince Vaughn, who also produced the film, as Nick Barrow, and Hailee Steinfeld as his estranged daughter Cate, with Bill Paxton, Jonathan Banks, Mike Epps, Jordi Mollà, Shea Whigham, William Levy, Taraji P. Henson, Annabeth Gish and Terrence Howard. Production was briefly halted when Universal canceled the film in 2013, but it was revived by QED International and PalmStar Entertainment and shot in Georgia in 2014.

Nick Barrow is a professional who plans heists and sells them to the highest bidder. When a job goes badly wrong, he finds himself framed and hunted, and he is forced to go on the run with Cate, a teenage daughter he has never really been part of the life of. Cate, whose mother is an alcoholic, has learned to fend for herself and resents her father for dragging her into his dangerous world.

As they flee, Nick tries to work out who double-crossed him, and with the help of an old acquaintance he concludes that a corrupt police officer, Keenan, wants him dead. Hunted by mob bosses, contract killers and dirty cops, and convinced he may not survive, Nick takes out a life insurance policy on himself so that Cate will be provided for once he is gone. Along the way, father and daughter slowly bond: Nick teaches her the tricks of his trade and how to survive, and Cate learns that he has secretly followed her life for years. As the danger closes in, Cate's own resourcefulness becomes key to their survival.

The film is a crime thriller built around a reluctant father-daughter relationship and the idea of a parent trying to make amends.

Term Life was released on April 29, 2016, in a limited release and on video on demand by Focus World. It received negative reviews, scoring 0 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from a handful of reviews, though the Los Angeles Times described it as cleanly plotted and tautly paced, if never as fun as it should be.

title: Tapped Out
tagline: He lost everything... except the will to fight
overview: A disgruntled teenager, sent to do community service at a rundown Karate school, enters an MMA tournament to face the man who killed his parents.
plot:
Tapped Out is a 2014 martial arts action drama directed by Allan Ungar, starring Cody Hackman as Michael Shaw, a young karate fighter seeking revenge for his parents' murder, with Michael Biehn as his mentor, Reggie Monroe, Krzysztof Soszynski as fighter Dominic Grey, Martin Kove, and mixed martial arts champions Anderson Silva and Lyoto Machida.

At twelve, Michael is a karate prodigy. On the way home from earning his brown belt, his parents' car is hijacked by two armed men, and one of them shoots both parents dead without noticing Michael hiding in the back seat; the boy sees a distinctive tattoo on the killer's neck and slips away when the car stops. Seven years later, Michael is a troubled teenager living with his grandfather. After trouble at a party he is sentenced to community service at a struggling karate school run by Reggie, a friend of his late father, and slowly rediscovers his love for the discipline. Reggie's niece, Jen, takes him to a local mixed martial arts event, and there Michael recognizes one of the fighters, Dominic Grey, as his parents' killer.

The police cannot act without evidence, the promoter, Lou, refuses to let him into the circuit, and when Michael follows Grey home with a gun, he cannot pull the trigger. Learning of a tournament whose winner will face Grey for $50,000, Michael accepts Reggie's offer to train him, without revealing his aim, and forces his way into the event by beating Lou's bodyguard. Their partnership breaks down when Reggie learns what he is doing, but after Jen explains Michael's motive, Reggie trains him with help from Silva and Machida, and the night before the fight he gives Michael the black belt his father had expected him to earn. Michael defeats every opponent with his karate and, before the final, announces that he witnessed the murder, prompting Grey and his manager to plan to kill him in the cage. The manager locks out the referee, and Grey nearly chokes Michael to death, but the sight of his parents in the crowd revives him. Remembering Reggie's advice, Michael spares Grey by breaking his leg instead of killing him and gives the prize money to Reggie's school, later laying his black belt on his parents' grave after Grey confesses and is imprisoned.

title: Alien Abduction
tagline: Fear The Lights...
overview: A vacationing family encounters an alien threat in this pulse-pounding thriller based on the real-life Brown Mountain Lights phenomenon in North Carolina.
plot:
Alien Abduction is a 2014 American found-footage sci-fi horror film, the first feature directed by Matty Beckerman, from a script by Robert Lewis. Riley Polanski plays Riley Morris, an autistic 11-year-old who films his family's encounter with aliens, with Katherine Sigismund and Peter Holden as his parents, Corey Eid and Jillian Clare as his siblings and Jeff Bowser as Sean, a mountain recluse. It was released on demand in April 2014.

The film opens with a shadowy figure walking a camera down a corridor filled with screams and dropping it through a chute into Earth orbit. On-screen text presents the recovered footage as part of Project Blue Book, documenting the disappearance of 27 people near Brown Mountain, North Carolina, in 2011. Riley, who keeps a video diary, is camping there with his father Peter, mother Katie, brother Corey and sister Jillian. On the first night the children watch three motionless lights in the sky that suddenly move off and vanish.

The next morning their GPS leads them astray on a fog-bound mountain road, their phones lose signal and the car runs short of fuel. They reach a tunnel blocked by abandoned cars whose occupants seem to have been dragged out. Peter sees an inhuman silhouette approaching, tells the boys to run and vanishes in a burst of light. When the rest of the family tries to drive off, a flock of crows rains onto the car and it dies. They take refuge with Sean, a hostile hermit who changes his mind when something attacks his guard dog, and who tells them that the lights and abductions have plagued the mountain for centuries. Sean leaves to search for his abducted brother, and when the cabin is breached Corey hides the others in the cellar and is taken. Sean returns and tries to drive them down the mountain, but the aliens catch up, seizing Katie and Sean at a barn. Riley and Jillian hide in the woods overnight, but the road they find at dawn leads back to the tunnel. A police officer arrives, but he, Jillian and Riley, still clutching his camera, are abducted, and the footage rises into orbit. Air Force personnel in hazmat suits recover the fallen camera. A year later, a state trooper finds Peter alive, naked and in shock on a bridge.

Beckerman drew on a North Carolina legend of mysterious lights and abductions. Reviews were mixed, with 29% on Rotten Tomatoes and 46 on Metacritic; critics liked Riley's use of the camera as a coping mechanism but found the plot generic.

title: A Monster Calls
tagline: Stories are wild creatures.
overview: A boy imagines a monster that helps him deal with his difficult life and see the world in a different way.
plot:
A Monster Calls is a 2016 dark fantasy drama directed by J. A. Bayona, with a screenplay by Patrick Ness adapted from his own 2011 novel of the same name. Lewis MacDougall leads the cast as Conor O'Malley, alongside Sigourney Weaver, Felicity Jones, Toby Kebbell and Liam Neeson, who provides the voice and motion capture for the title creature. The film is a Spanish, British and American co-production, with Focus Features acquiring the rights in 2014.

Set in rural England, the story follows twelve-year-old Conor, whose mother is undergoing chemotherapy for a serious illness. Conor dislikes his rigid grandmother and dreads the idea of living with her, since his father has started a new family in the United States. At school he is bullied by a classmate named Harry, and at night he is haunted by a recurring nightmare in which the old church near his house collapses into a pit and he struggles to keep his mother from falling in. He copes by drawing, a talent he inherited from his mother.

One night, at seven minutes past midnight, the ancient yew tree beside the church comes to life as a towering Monster. It announces that it will tell Conor three stories over its coming visits, and that afterwards Conor must tell it a fourth story: the truth behind his nightmare. The Monster's tales, rendered in watercolour-style animation, are morally ambiguous fables about a prince and a queen, an apothecary and a parson, and an invisible man, each one refusing to offer the simple lessons Conor expects. As his mother's health declines and he is forced to move into his grandmother's house, Conor's grief and anger begin to spill into destructive outbursts, while a visit from his father brings more disappointment than comfort.

The film builds toward Conor's confrontation with the real meaning of his dream, in which he must admit the conflicted feelings he has been hiding: his wish for the pain of waiting to end, and the guilt that comes with it. Through this admission the story explores how children process loss, the coexistence of love and resentment, and the value of telling the truth.

A Monster Calls was praised for MacDougall's performance, Neeson's voice work, its visual effects and its emotional honesty, and it won several Goya Awards, including Best Director for Bayona.

title: Carol

plot:
Carol is a 2015 American romantic drama film directed by Todd Haynes, based on Patricia Highsmith's semi-autobiographical novel The Price of Salt. The film stars Cate Blanchett as Carol Aird and Rooney Mara as Therese Belivet.

The story begins in New York City in the summer of 1952. We meet Carol Aird (Cate Blanchett), a wealthy socialite who has just arrived from Europe, where she was married to Harge Aird (Kyle Chandler). The marriage is loveless, and Carol is eager to escape her husband's suffocating grasp.

While exploring the city, Carol meets Therese Belivet (Rooney Mara), a young salesgirl at a department store. Their initial encounter is brief, but it sparks an undeniable connection between them. As they continue to cross paths, their conversations become more meaningful, and they begin to develop feelings for each other.

As the summer progresses, Carol and Therese's relationship deepens, despite the societal norms that prohibit same-sex relationships in 1950s America. They share stolen moments together, exchanging letters and gifts, and exploring the city's hidden corners.

However, their love is threatened by the constraints of Carol's marriage and the expectations of her family and friends. Harge Aird returns from Europe, unaware of Carol's growing feelings for Therese, and demands that she return to their home in the Hamptons.

Carol is torn between her duty to her husband and her desire for freedom and love with Therese. As the summer draws to a close, Carol must make a choice between conforming to societal norms or risking everything to be with the woman she loves.

The film's climax features a poignant and heart-wrenching confrontation between Carol and Harge Aird, which ultimately leads to Carol's decision to leave her husband and start a new life with Therese. The ending is bittersweet, as Carol must navigate the challenges of being an openly gay woman in a society that rejects her.

Throughout the film, Haynes masterfully captures the atmosphere of 1950s America, with its strict social norms and repressive attitudes towards same-sex relationships. The cinematography is stunning, with a muted color palette that evokes the melancholy and longing of Carol's story.

Cate Blanchett delivers a tour-de-force performance as Carol Aird, bringing depth and nuance to a character who is both strong-willed and vulnerable. Rooney Mara shines as Therese Belivet, capturing the innocence and passion of a young woman falling in love for the first time.

Overall, Carol is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of love, identity, and freedom in a society that seeks to constrain them. With its stunning performances, poignant script, and masterful direction, it is a must-see for anyone who loves great storytelling and powerful performances.

plot:
The Legend of Tarzan is a 2016 American adventure film directed by David Yates, based on the classic novel "Tarzan" by Edgar Rice Burroughs. The movie stars Alexander Skarsgård as Tarzan, Margot Robbie as Jane Porter, and Christoph Waltz as Lord Greystoke.

The film begins with a young boy named John Clayton (Alexander Skarsgård), who is raised by gorillas in the jungle after his parents' death. He is found by a gorilla named Kala, who adopts him and teaches him how to survive in the jungle. As John grows up, he learns about the ways of the wild and becomes a skilled hunter and warrior.

Years later, Lord Greystoke (Christoph Waltz), John's father, is captured by a group of poachers led by Medusa (Samuel L. Jackson). The poachers plan to sell him as a slave, but they are thwarted by a group of rebels who rescue Greystoke and return him to England.

In England, Greystoke marries Lady Alice (Diana Hardcastle) and has a son named John Clayton. However, the marriage is unhappy, and Lady Alice dies soon after giving birth to their son. Lord Greystoke becomes ill and dies, leaving John as the sole heir to his title and estate.

The film then jumps forward in time, where we see John Clayton (Alexander Skarsgård) living a life of luxury as the Earl of Greystoke. However, he is unhappy with his life and feels disconnected from his heritage. He meets Jane Porter (Margot Robbie), a beautiful and adventurous young woman who has come to Africa on an expedition.

As John and Jane spend more time together, they begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that John is hiding his true identity as Tarzan, the jungle boy raised by gorillas.

Meanwhile, Medusa (Samuel L. Jackson) returns with a group of mercenaries who are seeking revenge against Greystoke for foiling their plans in the past. They kidnap Jane and take her to the jungle, where they plan to use her as leverage to get to John.

Tarzan must then confront his past and face Medusa's men in order to rescue Jane and protect his home in the jungle. Along the way, he also learns more about his father's death and the reason behind his adoption by the gorillas.

In the end, Tarzan defeats Medusa and his men, and he and Jane confess their love for each other. The film ends with John Clayton embracing his true identity as Tarzan, and he and Jane setting off on a new adventure together in the jungle.

Overall, The Legend of Tarzan is an action-packed adventure film that explores themes of identity, belonging, and redemption. The movie features stunning visuals, impressive stunts, and a strong performance from Alexander Skarsgård as the titular character.

Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Road Chip is a 2015 American musical comedy directed by Walt Becker and written by Randi Mayem Singer and Adam Sztykiel, the fourth film in the live-action and computer-animated Alvin and the Chipmunks series. It opened in North America on December 18, 2015.

Alvin, Simon and Theodore throw Dave a birthday party that grows out of control, much to his annoyance. When he takes them mini-golfing they meet his girlfriend Samantha, whom they like, and her teenage son Miles, who bullies them. Later the Chipmunks find an engagement ring among Dave's belongings and conclude he is about to propose, which would make Miles their stepbrother. Dave leaves to produce a record for the singer Ashley Grey in Miami, taking Samantha with him and leaving the boys with Miles, so the four decide to travel to Miami and stop the proposal, leaving drugged squirrels dressed in their clothes to fool the neighbour.

On the plane, Theodore frees the animals in the cargo hold, forcing an emergency landing in Austin, Texas, and drawing the wrath of the Air Marshal James Suggs, who holds a grudge against the Chipmunks and puts them on the no-fly list. After escaping him in a bar brawl and being thrown out of a cab, Miles opens up about his father abandoning him, and the four begin to bond. They busk their way to New Orleans and perform in a Mardi Gras parade, which is broadcast on live television, and get Suggs drunk on moonshine. Dave and Samantha catch up with them at the airport, angry at their disobedience, and drive them the rest of the way to Miami.

In Miami, Alvin reveals that he has stolen the ring, but Miles, now fond of the Chipmunks, is upset, and when he wanders into traffic, the Chipmunks save his life. They resolve to return the ring and tell Dave that they accept Samantha and Miles, only to learn that the ring belongs to Dave's friend Barry, who was planning his own proposal. The boys perform a new song at the record's launch party, Barry's proposal succeeds, and Dave formally adopts the Chipmunks, although the squirrels have wrecked his house.

Wrong Turn 6: Last Resort, styled on screen as Wrong Turn VI, is a 2014 slasher film directed by Valeri Milev and the sixth installment in the Wrong Turn series, which it reboots. Milev replaced Declan O'Brien after plans for a film completing a prequel trilogy that began with Wrong Turn 5: Bloodlines were dropped, and shooting reportedly began in Bulgaria in March 2014. 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment released it on DVD and digital platforms on October 21, 2014.

In the West Virginia hills, a pair of bikers are murdered by the cannibal Hillicker brothers, Three Finger, Saw Tooth and One Eye, who are looked after by their deranged kin Jackson and Sally, caretakers of the remote Hobb Springs resort. Danny arrives to claim an unexpected inheritance, accompanied by his girlfriend, Toni, her brother, Rod, and friends Vic, Charlie, Bryan and Bryan's girlfriend, Jillian. Meanwhile an elderly guest, Agnes Fields, is killed with an axe. When Sheriff Doucette warns Bryan and Jillian that townspeople and hotel guests have been disappearing, he is killed at a roadblock by Three Finger. The friends grow suspicious of Danny's cousins, and Danny's growing attachment to his newfound family strains his relationships with the others, though they reluctantly stay when he plans to reopen the hotel.

Planning to leave, Bryan and Jillian steal valuables and find a hidden bathhouse beneath the hotel, where the cannibals ambush them; Jillian is dismembered, and Bryan, left brain-damaged, is assaulted and smothered by Sally. Jackson and Sally reveal to Danny that he is a Hillicker and introduce him to his cannibal relatives, while Vic, who followed them, is captured and disemboweled for the clan's feast. The survivors discover Jackson cooking their friends' remains, and Charlie and Rod are killed as they try to flee. Toni arms herself with a rifle, maims Sally in a fight and kills Jackson with the door keys after Danny lets her go, but Danny, furious at Jackson's death, lets the cannibals kill her. A year later the reopened resort, now Hillicker Springs, is managed by Danny, who carries on the family's sordid traditions with Sally.

Anthony Ilott plays Danny, with Aqueela Zoll as Toni, Chris Jarvis as Jackson and Sadie Katz as Sally. Reviews were negative: Dread Central's Steve Barton gave it 1.5 out of 5 while praising Katz, though Starburst's Joel Harley called it one of the best entries yet. It earned about $1 million in home sales before Wrong Turn (2021) followed.

plot:
Joy Ride 3: Roadkill, also known as Joy Ride 3, is a 2014 American direct-to-video horror film written and directed by Declan O'Brien. It stars Ken Kirzinger as the murderous trucker Rusty Nail, with Jesse Hutch, Kirsten Prout, Ben Hollingsworth and Dean Armstrong. A sequel to Joy Ride (2001) and Joy Ride 2: Dead Ahead (2008), it is the third and final installment in the series and was released digitally and on DVD in June 2014.

In a motel room, a drug-addicted couple, Rob and Candy, use a CB radio to lure a trucker to their door so they can rob him, but the man who answers is Rusty Nail. He takes them captive, chains them to the axle of his truck and offers them freedom if they can hold onto the hood for a mile along a deserted stretch of Highway 17, a sadistic game that ends with both of them dead. A newly appointed deputy, Officer Williams, wants to look into the case, but Officer Jenkins encourages the deputy to treat it as an open-and-shut case. Meanwhile, a team of racecar drivers, including Jordon and Austin, Jordon's girlfriend Jewel and teammates Mickey, Alisa and Bobby, are traveling to Canada to compete in the Road Rally 1000. At a roadside diner Austin spots an unpatrolled shortcut that could save them a day, and although an old trucker named Barry warns them that the road is known as "Slaughter Alley" and tells them the legend of Rusty Nail, they decide to take it anyway, since the empty highway also lets them test their car. On the road, an irritated Austin taunts a passing trucker who turns out to be Rusty Nail, and the killer soon retaliates, running their trailer off the road and using the camera on his rig to identify Jordon's license plate. Over the CB radio he vows revenge, and as night falls he begins to hunt the racers one by one, running Jewel and Austin off the road as they head for the police and abducting them, before demanding the team's racecar as ransom, and the rest of the group, picked off one by one, struggles to rescue their friends and escape the highway alive.

The cast also includes Leela Savasta as Alisa and Gianpaolo Venuta as Austin. The film earned more than $1.28 million in home video sales.

plot:
Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them is a 2016 fantasy film directed by David Yates and written by J. K. Rowling, her first screenplay. The opening entry in the Fantastic Beasts series and the ninth film in the Wizarding World franchise, it serves as a spin-off and prequel to the Harry Potter films, inspired by the guide book Rowling published in 2001 under the name of its fictional author, Newt Scamander, to benefit Comic Relief. Chasing an escaped Niffler, he accidentally swaps cases with Jacob Kowalski, a non-magical would-be baker, and is detained by Tina Goldstein, a demoted Auror of the Magical Congress of the United States (MACUSA). Meanwhile a destructive force rampages through the city and kills Senator Henry Shaw Jr. MACUSA blames an Obscurial, a dark parasitic force born of suppressed magic, found in Newt's case, and security director Percival Graves sentences Newt and Tina to death, but Queenie helps them escape.

Aurors destroy the Obscurial after Newt and Tina try to calm him, and Newt exposes Graves as the dark wizard Gellert Grindelwald in disguise. Newt's Thunderbird spreads a rain that wipes the city's memories, seemingly including Jacob's, yet he later opens a bakery with silver eggshells Newt gave him and smiles in recognition when Queenie walks in.

Eddie Redmayne plays Newt, with Katherine Waterston, Dan Fogler, Alison Sudol, Ezra Miller, Samantha Morton and Colin Farrell. plot:
The Conjuring 2 is a 2016 American supernatural horror film directed by James Wan and written by Wan and Leigh Whannell. It is the sequel to The Conjuring (2013) and the third installment in The Conjuring Universe.

The film takes place in 1977, six months after the events of the first film. Ed and Lorraine Warren (Patrick Wilson and Vera Farmiga), paranormal investigators, are called to London by a family who claims that their home is haunted by a malevolent spirit. The family, consisting of Peggy Hodgson (Shanley Caswell) and her five children, has been experiencing terrifying events, including unexplained noises, movements, and possessions.

Upon arrival, the Warrens begin to investigate the haunting, which they believe is connected to a dark entity that was once a patient at a nearby psychiatric hospital. The entity, known as Bathsheba, was a 16-year-old girl who was institutionalized for her alleged demonic possession in the 1950s. The Warrens soon discover that Bathsheba's spirit has been awakened by a series of events, including the family's recent move into the new home.

As the investigation progresses, Ed and Lorraine begin to experience strange occurrences themselves, which they attribute to the entity's presence. They also uncover evidence of Bathsheba's dark past, including her history of abuse and trauma. The Warrens soon realize that Bathsheba is not just a simple spirit but a malevolent force that has been awakened by the family's own emotional turmoil.

The film builds up to a climactic confrontation between the Warrens and Bathsheba, which takes place in the abandoned psychiatric hospital where she was once institutionalized. The entity unleashes its full fury on the Warrens, who must use all their skills and knowledge to defeat her.

Throughout the film, Wan expertly crafts tension and suspense, using a combination of jump scares, creepy atmosphere, and clever plot twists to keep the audience on edge. The Conjuring 2 is also notable for its strong female lead, Lorraine Warren, who takes center stage in this installment.

The film received widespread critical acclaim, with many praising Wan's direction and the performances of the cast. The Conjuring 2 was a commercial success, grossing over $320 million worldwide and cementing the Conjuring Universe as a major player in the horror genre.

Overall, The Conjuring 2 is a chilling and well-crafted horror film that explores themes of trauma, abuse, and the supernatural. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and expert direction, it is a must-see for fans of the horror genre.

As the story progresses, Alice starts to realize that she needs to focus on herself and figure out what makes her happy. She takes a break from dating and focuses on her career and friendships. Along the way, she meets a new guy named Tom (Pete Davidson), who is quirky and charming.

The movie's plot development is driven by Alice's journey of self-discovery. As she navigates her love life and tries to figure out what she wants to do with her life, she learns valuable lessons about herself and the importance of being true to oneself.

She says goodbye to Ben and moves on to new experiences and relationships. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Alice feeling more confident and self-assured than ever before.

Overall, How to Be Single is a fun and relatable romantic comedy that explores the ups and downs of dating in your 20s. With its talented cast and witty dialogue, it's a must-see for anyone who has ever navigated the challenges of love and relationships.

title: Coming Home
overview: Lu and Feng are a devoted couple forced to separate when Lu is arrested and sent to a labor camp as a political prisoner during the Cultural Revolution. He finally returns home only to find that his beloved wife no longer remembers him.
plot:
Coming Home (Chinese: 归来, literally "The Return") is a 2014 Chinese historical drama film directed by Zhang Yimou. It stars Chen Daoming as Lu Yanshi, Gong Li as his wife Feng Wanyu and Zhang Huiwen as their daughter Dandan. The story is adapted from Geling Yan's novel The Criminal Lu Yanshi, a family chronicle about Chinese intellectuals persecuted during the Cultural Revolution; the screenplay draws only on the final 20 pages of the roughly 400-page book.

Lu Yanshi, a former professor, has been sent to a labor camp during the Cultural Revolution. He escapes from the camp in Xining hoping to see his wife Feng Wanyu and their daughter Dandan, whom he has not seen in years, but the police are already watching the family home. Dandan, a teenage ballet student, has been denied the lead role in a production of The Red Detachment of Women because of her father's status as a fugitive. Tempted by the promise of regaining the part, she tells the authorities about her parents' planned secret meeting. Lu is captured, yet Dandan still does not receive the role.

When the Cultural Revolution ends, Lu is finally allowed to return home, but he finds his family shattered. Dandan now works in a textile factory, and Feng suffers from a form of amnesia that leaves her unable to recognize her husband. Traumatized by sexual harassment from a former official, she sometimes mistakes Lu for that man, Officer Fang. Determined to reawaken her memory, Lu stays close to her in a series of guises, posing as a stranger who reads letters to her or as a piano tuner, though her trauma keeps him from ever truly living with her again. Over the years he continues to write letters to Feng, using them as a way to communicate with her and to persuade her to forgive their daughter. Years later, on a snowy day, Feng is still waiting outside the railway station for her husband to arrive, with Lu standing beside her, pretending to be a pedicab driver.

The film was first shown publicly at the Cannes Film Festival on 20 May 2014 and was released in the United States on September 11, 2015. Critics praised its heartbreaking portrait of ordinary lives shattered by political upheaval, Gong Li's performance and Zhang's return to understated storytelling, although some felt it held back from deeper historical reflection, a restraint often attributed to censorship. It grossed ¥23.7 million on its first day in China and about US$49.7 million in total.

plot:
Monster High: Frights, Camera, Action! is a 2014 American computer-animated fantasy film based on Mattel's Monster High fashion doll franchise, whose characters are teenage children of classic horror monsters. Directed by William Lau, it was animated by the Vancouver studio Nerd Corps Entertainment for Mattel Entertainment, as part of the franchise's first generation of 3D films. The voice cast includes Debi Derryberry, Salli Saffioti, Julie Maddalena, Kate Higgins, Karen Strassman and Laura Bailey.

The story revolves around a centuries-old legend about a missing vampire queen and a long-lost stone known as the Vampire's Heart. The vampire community has had no queen for 400 years, ever since the last heir, Elissabat, ran away on the day of her coronation, and the legend has inspired a popular, melodramatic movie franchise, Vampire Majesty, in which two suitors compete for the queen. Draculaura, whose family once belonged to the vampire court, dislikes how the films depict vampire royalty. When the vampire council demands that the interim ruler, the greedy Lord Stoker, produce the missing heir within a week, he convinces Draculaura that she is the rightful heir in order to manipulate her, and even tries to force her to marry him. She and her best friends are whisked off to Transylvania for the coronation, but they soon discover that the search for the true queen is not over. Hunting for the Vampire's Heart, Draculaura, Cleo de Nile, Robecca and Hoodude Voodoo follow clues to New Goreleans, Londoom and Barcelgroana, picking up new friends along the way: the aspiring cinematographer Honey Swamp, the screenwriting student Clawdia Wolf and the makeup artist Viperine Gorgon. The trail ends in the film capital Hauntlywood, where the famous actress Veronica Von Vamp is rumored to know where Elissabat is. Back at school, the students hold a "cute court" to decide which vampire actor is more attractive.

Universal Pictures Home Entertainment released the film on DVD and Blu-ray on 25 March 2014, with three 2D animated shorts as extras. Reviews were moderate. High Def Digest found it less catchy than the previous entry, with a slow middle section, but enjoyed its jabs at pop culture and the Twilight craze and its strong, funny finale in Hauntlywood, recommending it mainly to fans. Common Sense Media found the plot amusing in spoofing fan debates over fictional love triangles, but rated it for ages eight and up because of its focus on teen crushes.

title: Bermuda Tentacles
overview: After Air Force One goes down during a storm over the Bermuda Triangle, the United States Navy is dispatched to find the escape pod holding the President. A giant monster beneath the ocean awakens and attacks the fleet.
plot:
Bermuda Tentacles is a 2014 American made-for-television science fiction action horror film directed by Nick Lyon and produced by The Asylum for the Syfy channel. Linda Hamilton heads a cast that also includes Trevor Donovan, Mýa, John Savage and Jamie Kennedy, in a story about a naval rescue mission in the Bermuda Triangle that runs into gigantic tentacled creatures of alien origin. It premiered on Syfy in April 2014.

While Air Force One is flying through a storm over the Bermuda Triangle, a massive lightning strike knocks out its engines, and President DeSteno is placed in a high-tech escape pod, given a gun and jettisoned moments before the plane explodes. The pod sinks some 7,000 metres to the ocean floor, and with his air supply limited, the Navy dispatches a fleet and an elite special forces team to retrieve him. The team, led by the reckless young Chief Trip Oliver, reports to Admiral Hansen, with whom Oliver shares a history of friction. Before a rescue can be planned, the ships are attacked by enormous translucent tentacles rising from the sea, which snatch and impale sailors and swat helicopters and planes out of the sky, while even larger squid-like limbs join the assault. The ship's scientist, Dr. Zimmer, quickly identifies the creatures as giant tube worms, and only concentrated firepower seems to harm them. Oliver's unit descends in an experimental submersible, following the pod's beacon into a vast undersea chamber filled with ships and aircraft lost in the Triangle over the centuries, and realise they have found the cause of the disappearances. Fighting off more tentacles, they rescue the president, though most of the team is killed. They then discover that the "city" is in fact a colossal alien spacecraft, which rises from the ocean and heads for the Florida coast, destroying naval vessels as it goes, while the president pushes for all-out war. Oliver devises a plan to stop it, and a well-placed rocket fired into the ship's core destroys it before it reaches land.

Hamilton plays Hansen, with Donovan as Oliver, Mýa as Lieutenant Plummer, Savage as DeSteno and Kennedy as Zimmer. Critics panned the film. HorrorNews.Net's Shawn Handling criticised its acting, writing, effects and score, concluding that it deserved to be sunk with the Triangle's missing ships, and Dread Central compared it unfavourably with Deep Rising, The Abyss and Independence Day, describing it as repetitive and short on imagination.

The children, Violet and Dash, are dealing with their own personal issues - Violet is trying to navigate her teenage years while hiding her superpowers from her peers, and Dash is struggling to control his speed.

As the story progresses, we see the Parr family facing various challenges and obstacles, including a confrontation with the villainous Underminer (a character from the first film). The family also receives help from Frozone (Lucius Best), who becomes an ally in their quest to stop the Screenslaver.

Ultimately, Elastigirl emerges victorious, but not before realizing that her family's happiness and well-being are more important than her superhero reputation. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with the Parr family reunited and ready to face whatever challenges come their way.

Throughout the film, Pixar explores themes of identity, family, and the importance of finding balance between personal and professional lives. The animation is stunning, with vibrant colors and intricate details that bring the characters and world to life.

The story moves back and forth between two timelines. In 1955 the Hollywood producer Mike Todd is struggling to assemble an international cast for Around the World in 80 Days, unable to pay the stars he wants. In 1931 Mario Moreno is a penniless drifter living out of a suitcase, taking odd jobs and failing as a boxer and as a bullfighter before landing work as a janitor for a small stage company. Pushed on stage, his first routine flops, but when he bickers with a heckler who has hurled a shoe at him, his rapid, roundabout patter wins the audience over, the verbal style that would later be called cantinflear. Thrown out after an awkward encounter with his boss's daughter, he is spotted by Estanislao Shilinsky, a figure in the Mexico City theatre world, who brings him to the capital. There he causes friction by improvising his lines and falls for fellow performer Valentina Ivanovna, whom he marries. In 1933 a drunk heckler's taunt gives him his stage name.

In the 1950s strand, Todd flies to Mexico City, watches Moreno perform in a bullring and hands him the script, but Moreno refuses, unwilling to leave his country or work for a studio; Charlie Chaplin later advises Todd on how to win him over. Meanwhile, Moreno's fame grows through political satire on stage and, from 1940, a hugely successful film career, along with union activism, while his marriage suffers from neglect and Valentina learns she cannot have children. After she walks out on him at a premiere at the Teatro de los Insurgentes, a drunken Moreno reads Todd's script and accepts. He reaches Los Angeles just as Todd is about to be fired, reconciles with Valentina, turns down further Hollywood work so he can stay among his people and adopt a child with her, and wins the Golden Globe for Best Actor in a Musical or Comedy.

Reviews were mixed, with 48% on Rotten Tomatoes and 45 on Metacritic, though Jaenada's performance was praised. The film won three Ariel Awards from five nominations.

title: Sorry If I Call You Love
overview: A successful, attractive, intelligent and brilliant advertising executive is longing to finally find emotional stability in his life, and decides to propose to his girlfriend. After she refuses his proposal, his life takes a turn when a new young lady enters his life.
plot:
Sorry If I Call You Love (Spanish: Perdona si te llamo amor) is a 2014 Spanish romantic drama film directed by Joaquín Llamas. Written by Fran Araújo and Manuel Burque, it adapts the 2007 novel of the same name by the Italian author Federico Moccia, which had already been filmed in Italy in 2008. A Telecinco Cinema production, it was shot in 2013 in Barcelona, Cadaqués and Paris, and was released in Spanish cinemas by Emon on 20 June 2014. It runs about 105 minutes and stars Paloma Bloyd and the Italian actor Daniele Liotti.

Liotti plays Alex, a handsome and successful 37-year-old advertising executive who, after years of hesitation, decides to settle down and proposes to his girlfriend Elena (Irene Montalà), only to be turned down. Shaken, he is distracted at the wheel and lightly knocks over Niki (Bloyd), a spirited 17-year-old in her final year of secondary school, who is riding a scooter. Niki charms him with her cheek and vitality, has him drive her wherever she likes, and soon persuades him into something he had never imagined: a romance with a woman twenty years his junior. The story is framed by the narration of a secretive detective.

The relationship brings the couple joy and plenty of trouble. Alex's colleagues at the agency insist on meeting Niki's friends, leading to a group date with mixed results; Niki, after her friends suggest that Alex might be secretly married, follows him and smashes his car window in a jealous rage on seeing him with a woman who turns out to be his sister. After a schoolmate of Niki's mocks Alex as a "grandpa" and punches him at a nightclub, he begins to doubt whether the age gap can be bridged. A romantic trip to Paris for Niki's eighteenth birthday briefly restores their hopes, but back home Alex ends the affair, saying they come from different worlds, and Niki calls him a coward. Weeks later he realises he cannot live without her, and the two are reunited on a holiday island.

The supporting cast includes Andrea Duro, Cristina Brondo, Jan Cornet and Pablo Chiapella. Critics were largely unimpressed. Pere Vall of Fotogramas awarded it two stars out of five, singling out Bloyd, her friends, Chiapella, the cinematography and the Barcelona setting amid many laughable scenes, while Jonathan Holland of The Hollywood Reporter called it a slick, superficial forbidden-love fantasy whose calculated lack of irony gave it a certain appeal.

title: Good People
tagline: Money changes everything
overview: Tom and Anna Wright, a young American couple, fall into severe debt while renovating Anna's family home in London. As the couple faces the loss of their dream to have a house and start a family, they discover that the tenant in the apartment below them is dead, and he's left behind a stash of cash—$400,000 worth. Though initially hesitant, Tom and Anna decide that the plan is simple: all they have to do is quietly take the money and use only what's necessary to get them out of debt. But when they start spending the money and can't seem to stop, they find themselves the target of a deadly adversary—the thief who stole it—and that's when very bad things start happening to good people.
plot:
Good People, released in some countries as Getaway 2, is a 2014 American action thriller film directed by Henrik Ruben Genz and written by Kelly Masterson, based on Marcus Sakey's 2008 novel of the same name. James Franco and Kate Hudson star as Tom and Anna Wright, an American couple in London who fall deep into debt while renovating a family home, with Omar Sy as the French heroin dealer Khan, Tom Wilkinson as Detective Inspector John Halden, Anna Friel as Anna's friend Sarah, Sam Spruell as Jack Witkowski and Diarmaid Murtagh as his accomplice Marshall.

Four men rob Khan of his drugs and money, but as they leave, Ben Tuttle shoots his partner Bobby and escapes with the entire haul, while Witkowski and Marshall flee empty-handed. Meanwhile, Tom and Anna, in debt and trying without success to have a baby, find their noisy downstairs tenant, Ben, dead of an apparent heroin overdose. Clearing his flat, they discover £220,000 hidden above a ceiling tile and, after some debate, spend it, Tom on paying off the house and Anna on fertility treatment. Detective Halden, who seems to connect Ben's death with that of his own daughter, suspects they are hiding something and starts following them. Witkowski kills Ben's cousin to learn Ben's address. Khan warns Tom that he must choose between him and Witkowski, and when Tom refuses, Witkowski tortures him for the money's location until Halden's arrival drives the criminals away. Because Witkowski has contacts inside the police, Halden proposes using the Wrights as bait in an unofficial operation. At the arranged money drop, Witkowski recognizes Halden as a policeman and Marshall shoots him, though a bulletproof vest saves his life, and the Wrights flee with the cash while Khan, believing he has been played, abandons them. Witkowski then takes Sarah and her baby hostage, and the Wrights agree to meet him at the house they had been renovating, which they rig with traps. Witkowski falls through the floor and Tom drives nails through Marshall's feet before Khan's men also arrive. In the chaos, Sarah and the baby escape, Khan kills Witkowski, Marshall's shot kills Khan, and Halden shoots Marshall as he is choking Anna. As the house burns down, the Wrights move out of their flat, and Anna tells Tom that she is pregnant.

Shot at Shepperton Studios and in London from June 2013, Good People was released in select cinemas and on demand on 26 September 2014. It was poorly received, with a 12% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

title: Insurgent
tagline: One Choice Can Destroy You
overview: Beatrice Prior must confront her inner demons and continue her fight against a powerful alliance which threatens to tear her society apart.
plot:
Insurgent is a 2015 science fiction action film directed by Robert Schwentke and written by Jon Hoeber, Eric Heisserer, and Michael Chabon. The movie is based on the novel "Divergent" by Veronica Roth.

The story takes place in a post-apocalyptic Chicago, where society is divided into five factions: Abnegation (selflessness), Amity (peacefulness), Candor (honesty), Dauntless (bravery), and Erudite (intelligence). The protagonist, Beatrice "Tris" Prior (Shailene Woodley), lives in Abnegation with her family. On the day of the annual Choosing Ceremony, where young adults choose their faction, Tris secretly takes the test for Dauntless.

During the test, Tris demonstrates exceptional bravery and skills, which makes her a strong candidate for Dauntless. However, she is also revealed to be Divergent, meaning she doesn't fit into any one faction. This puts her in danger, as the Erudite faction, led by Jeanine Matthews (Kate Winslet), seeks to eliminate all Divergents.

Tris begins her training at Dauntless under the guidance of Four (Ansel Elgort), a skilled instructor who becomes Tris's mentor and love interest. As she navigates her new life in Dauntless, Tris uncovers a plot by the Erudite to overthrow the government and take control of Chicago.

Tris soon discovers that her father, Andrew Prior (Tony Goldwyn), is involved with the Erudite and has been hiding secrets about their past. She also learns that she has a unique connection to the simulated world of "The Simulated Reality," which holds the key to understanding the Divergent phenomenon.

As Tris delves deeper into the mystery, she must confront her own identity and the true nature of her faction. With the help of Four and her fellow Dauntless initiates, Tris embarks on a perilous journey to uncover the truth about the Erudite's plans and save Chicago from destruction.

The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between Tris and Jeanine Matthews, with Tris using her unique skills and connection to the simulated world to outsmart the Erudite leader. In the end, Tris emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. The film concludes with Tris and Four parting ways, as they both embark on new paths, leaving the audience wondering what the future holds for these characters.

Overall, Insurgent is a thrilling sci-fi adventure that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and self-discovery in a dystopian world.
