title: Falcon Rising
overview: Chapman is an ex-marine in Brazil's slums, battling the yakuza outfit who attacked his sister and left her for dead.
plot:
John "Falcon" Chapman is a United States Marine Corps veteran who suffers from posttraumatic stress disorder. After playing Russian roulette, he enters a convenience store moments before it is robbed. He demands one of the robbers shoot him, and when the man hesitates, Chapman grows impatient, disarms the robbers, and foils the robbery. When he meets with his sister Cindy, who has briefly returned to New York for a wedding, she chastises him for not taking his medication and explains that she is returning to Brazil, where she has been doing charity work for a non-profit organization. Chapman receives word from Manny Ridley, a fellow veteran and diplomat, that his sister has been severely beaten. Chapman immediately leaves for Brazil.
Chapman meets Thiago Santo and his partner Carlo Bororo, who are investigating his sister's assault. Though no witnesses have come forward, Santo promises justice. Santo and Ridley warn Chapman to avoid the gangster-controlled favelas, but Chapman insists on performing his own investigation. Katarina Da Silva, a beat cop, shows Chapman where his sister was found. When Chapman visits his sister in the hospital, an Asian nurse administers medicine to Cindy's IV. Cindy goes into convulsions, and Chapman calls for help. The hospital says they have no Asian nurses, and Ridley suggests that the yakuza may be involved, as Brazil has a sizeable Japanese immigrant population.
Chapman returns to the favela and beats up several people when he notices one is wearing Cindy's necklace. Da Silva arrives and stops him, explaining that the man is Cindy's friend. Da Silva translates for him, and Chapman learns that Cindy gave her necklace to him after his sister disappeared. The man gives Chapman Cindy's torn journal, which he recovered, and Chapman apologizes. Using carbon paper, Chapman recovers a phone number and contacts another of Cindy's friends, a photographer, who explains that she was investigating corruption and a possible conspiracy involving human trafficking. When the photographer is unwilling to part with proof, Chapman pickpockets it. The photographer dies in a car bomb seconds later.
After engaging in a gun fight with yakuza gangsters, Chapman investigates a nightclub with yakuza ties. There, he beats up a Brazilian smuggler who works for Hirimoto, the yakuza boss. Ridley identifies official documents as fakes and the two realize the yakuza are kidnapping young girls from the favela and forcing them into prostitution. At the same time, Santo organizes a violent raid of the favela, killing many Brazilian drug dealers. When one of his officers stumbles onto a yakuza kidnapping, Santo kills the officer and demands double his pay from the yakuza. Chapman investigates a yakuza brothel, where he is recognized and beats up several gangsters. Santo is called to kill him, but when Da Silva also arrives, Santo is unable to do anything.

overview: Skipper, Kowalski, Rico and Private join forces with undercover organization The North Wind to stop the villainous Dr. Octavius Brine from destroying the world as we know it.
plot:
Penguins of Madagascar is a 2014 computer-animated spy comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie serves as a spin-off from the Madagascar franchise and follows the adventures of four penguin characters: Skipper, Kowalski, Rico, and Private.

The story begins with Skipper (Tom McGrath), the leader of the group, who is tasked with protecting the New York City Zoo's penguin exhibit. However, their lives are disrupted when a villainous octopus named Dave (John Malkovich) escapes from the aquarium and starts causing chaos in the city.

As the penguins try to stop Dave, they discover that he has stolen a valuable treasure map that leads to the legendary Golden Chalice of Africa. The chalice is said to have the power to grant any wish, and various villains are after it.

The penguins soon find themselves on a mission to retrieve the Golden Chalice before it falls into the wrong hands. Along the way, they team up with a new character, Classified (Benedict Cumberbatch), a top-secret agent who is sent to help them on their quest.

As the adventure unfolds, the penguins face various obstacles and challenges, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and rival treasure hunters. Through their teamwork and quick thinking, they are able to overcome these hurdles and stay one step ahead of their enemies.

Throughout the movie, the characters' personalities shine through in comedic moments, showcasing their unique skills and quirks. Skipper's leadership is put to the test as he tries to keep his team on track, while Kowalski's genius-level intellect helps them decipher clues and solve puzzles.

As the final showdown approaches, the penguins face off against Dave and his minions in an action-packed battle. In the end, they successfully retrieve the Golden Chalice and use its power to grant a wish that benefits the entire penguin community.

The movie concludes with the penguins returning home as heroes, hailed by their fellow penguins for their bravery and ingenuity. The film ends on a lighthearted note, with the characters enjoying a well-deserved celebration and looking forward to their next adventure together.

Overall, Penguins of Madagascar is a fun and entertaining animated film that showcases the unique personalities and skills of its lovable penguin characters. With its engaging storyline, witty humor, and stunning animation, it's a must-see for fans of the Madagascar franchise and comedy enthusiasts alike.

title: Captain America: Civil War
tagline: United we stand. Divided we fall.
overview: Following the events of Age of Ultron, the collective governments of the world pass an act designed to regulate all superhuman activity. This polarizes opinion amongst the Avengers, causing two factions to side with Iron Man or Captain America, which causes an epic battle between former allies.
plot:
Captain America: Civil War is a 2016 superhero film directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, based on the comic book storyline of the same name by Mark Millar and Steve McNiven. The movie takes place after the events of Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015) and follows the story of Captain America (Steve Rogers), Iron Man (Tony Stark), and their respective allies as they navigate a complex web of politics, morality, and personal relationships.

The film begins with the United Nations imposing the Sokovia Accords on the world's superheroes, requiring them to be registered and regulated by a governing body. The Accords are designed to prevent future catastrophes like Ultron from occurring, but many superheroes, including Captain America, oppose the measure, fearing it will lead to government control and undermine their autonomy.

Captain America, who has been traveling the world with his team, the Winter Soldier (Bucky Barnes), is summoned back to New York City for a United Nations hearing on the Sokovia Accords. There, he meets with Iron Man, who supports the Accords, and Black Widow (Natasha Romanoff), who is torn between her loyalty to Captain America and her duty to the government.

As tensions rise, the Avengers are divided into two factions: those in favor of the Accords, led by Iron Man, and those opposed, led by Captain America. The conflict escalates when Bucky Barnes, who has been presumed dead for years, is revealed to be alive and under the control of the Winter Soldier program.

The Winter Soldier, now a brainwashed assassin, is sent on a mission to kill Steve Rogers, but he is thwarted by Black Panther (T'Challa), Spider-Man (Peter Parker), Falcon (Sam Wilson), and Winter Soldier's own friend, Bucky Barnes. The team manages to escape, but not before the Winter Soldier kills several people, including a young girl.

The incident sparks a global outcry, and the Avengers are forced to go their separate ways. Captain America and his allies, including Black Panther, Falcon, and Spider-Man, form a new team, known as the "Winter Soldiers," while Iron Man and his allies, including Black Widow, War Machine (James Rhodes), and Spider-Man, form another team.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between the two teams in Leipzig-Halle Airport. The Winter Soldiers, led by Captain America, manage to defeat their opponents, but not before several people are killed, including Peter Parker's friend, Ned Leeds.

In the aftermath of the battle, Steve Rogers is forced to go into hiding, and Iron Man is left to deal with the consequences of his actions. The movie ends with a sense of uncertainty, as the world struggles to come to terms with the implications of the Sokovia Accords and the future of the Avengers.

Throughout the film, the Russo brothers explore themes of morality, responsibility, and the nature of heroism. Captain America's character is particularly nuanced, as he grapples with the consequences of his actions and the weight of his responsibilities as a leader. The movie also features memorable performances from the cast, including Chris Evans, Robert Downey Jr., Scarlett Johansson, and Chadwick Boseman.

Overall, Captain America: Civil War is a thought-provoking and action-packed film that sets the stage for the Marvel Cinematic Universe's next phase of storytelling.

title: Suite Française
tagline: Forced to host the enemy. Tormented by intruders. Tempted by desire.
overview: France, 1940. In the first days of occupation, beautiful Lucile Angellier is trapped in a stifled existence with her controlling mother-in-law as they both await news of her husband: a prisoner of war. Parisian refugees start to pour into their small town, soon followed by a regiment of German soldiers who take up residence in the villagers' own homes. Lucile initially tries to ignore Bruno von Falk, the handsome and refined German officer staying with them. But soon, a powerful love draws them together and leads them into the tragedy of war.
plot:
Suite Française is a 2015 war romance directed by Saul Dibb, who co-wrote the screenplay with Matt Charman, based on the second part of Irène Némirovsky's novel, written in the early 1940s and published posthumously in 2004. Michelle Williams stars as Lucile Angellier, with Kristin Scott Thomas as her mother-in-law, Matthias Schoenaerts as the German officer Bruno von Falk, Sam Riley, Ruth Wilson, Lambert Wilson and Margot Robbie. Filmed in France and Belgium, it was released in the United Kingdom in March 2015 and premiered in the United States on the Lifetime network in 2017.

In 1940, in the small French town of Bussy, Lucile lives with her domineering mother-in-law, Madame Angellier, while awaiting news of her husband, Gaston, who is serving in the French army. After surviving an air raid by German dive bombers while collecting rents from the family's tenants, the women learn of France's surrender, and soon a German regiment arrives and billets its soldiers in the villagers' homes. Oberleutnant Bruno von Falk, a cultured aristocrat and composer, is quartered at the Angellier house. Lucile tries to ignore him, but she is gradually drawn to his courteous manner and the music he plays on the piano.

Lucile learns that Gaston is being held in a German prisoner-of-war camp. Meanwhile the farmer Benoît, who was unable to fight because of a leg injury, and his wife Madeleine suffer under the harassment of another German officer, Kurt Bonnet, and Benoît secretly hides a rifle. When Lucile discovers that one of the tenants is sleeping with a German soldier, the woman reveals that Gaston had been having an affair and fathered a daughter. Angry that her mother-in-law kept the secret, Lucile grows closer to Bruno. As tensions rise between villagers and occupiers, with informers denouncing their neighbors, Benoît's resistance leads to violence, and Lucile is forced to choose between her feelings for Bruno and loyalty to her community, risking her life to help Benoît escape.

The film received mixed reviews, with praise for Williams's performance and its period detail but criticism that it reduced Némirovsky's sweeping novel to a conventional romance. Némirovsky, a Jewish writer, was deported and died at Auschwitz in 1942, and her manuscript was preserved by her daughters for decades.

title: Big Fish & Begonia

overview: Beyond the human realm, there is a magical race of beings who control the tides and the changing of the seasons. plot:

Meilu's life takes an unexpected turn when she meets a mysterious and handsome man named Bai Suzhen, who claims to be from a magical world called the "Begonia". According to legend, the Begonia is a realm where humans and plants coexist, and its inhabitants possess extraordinary abilities. Meilu is drawn to Bai's charming personality and sense of adventure, and she decides to follow him into the mystical forest.

As they journey deeper into the forest, Meilu discovers that the world of the Begonia is in danger due to a dark force known as the "White Lotus". The White Lotus is a malevolent entity that threatens to destroy the balance between humans and plants. Bai Suzhen reveals that he is on a quest to defeat the White Lotus and save his home.

Meilu joins forces with Bai, and together they embark on a perilous journey through treacherous landscapes and fantastical creatures. Along the way, Meilu learns about the history of the Begonia and its people, who possess unique abilities that allow them to communicate with plants.

As they near their destination, Meilu begins to realize that her own connection to the mystical world is more than just coincidence. She discovers that she has a special bond with the plants in the forest, which allows her to sense the emotions of those around her. This newfound understanding enables her to help Bai defeat the White Lotus and restore balance to the Begonia.

The film's climax features an epic battle between good and evil, as Meilu and Bai confront the dark force threatening their world. With the help of the plants and her own growing powers, Meilu is able to harness the energy of the forest and defeat the White Lotus.

In the aftermath of their victory, Meilu returns to her village, but she is forever changed by her experiences in the Begonia. She has discovered a new sense of purpose and belonging, and she realizes that her connection to the mystical world is more than just a coincidence – it's a part of who she truly is.

The film ends with Meilu standing at the edge of the forest, looking out at the world beyond. Though she has returned home, she knows that she will always carry the magic of the Begonia within her. The final shot is of the mystical realm, where Bai Suzhen remains, watching over Meilu and waiting for their next adventure together.

Overall, Big Fish & Begonia is a beautifully crafted tale of self-discovery, love, and the power of nature. With its stunning visuals, memorable characters, and epic storyline, this film is sure to captivate audiences and leave them enchanted by its magical world.

plot:
K: Missing Kings is a 2014 Japanese animated urban fantasy film directed by Shingo Suzuki, a sequel to the television anime K created by the writing collective GoRA. Set around a year after the events of the series, it bridges the first season and the second, K: Return of Kings. The Japanese voice cast includes Daisuke Namikawa, Daisuke Ono, Tomokazu Sugita, Mikako Komatsu, Kenjiro Tsuda, Takahiro Sakurai and Yui Horie, who voices the young girl Anna and also sings the insert song "Flames of Red". The music is by Mikio Endo.

The world of K is governed by seven Kings, each leading a clan of followers with supernatural powers. Almost a year has passed since the so-called Academy Island Incident, in which four of the Kings crossed paths and Mikoto Suoh, the Red King, was killed. His clan, HOMRA, has fallen into disarray, with several members gone their separate ways and Yata unable to let go of the past. Kuroh Yatogami and Neko, followers of the Silver King, have spent months searching without success for their missing master, Shiro, and are losing heart.

One day the two see HOMRA's Rikio Kamamoto and Anna Kushina being chased. The pursuers belong to the Green Clan, whose King sees the Silver King as the greatest threat to his plans and wants to kidnap Anna, believing that her gift for locating people will reveal whether Shiro is still alive and where he is. Defending her, Kuroh discovers that one of the Green Clan's most dangerous fighters, the flamboyant swordsman Yukari, was a fellow disciple of his former master, a man he once looked up to as an older brother. While Kuroh, Neko and Yata fight to rescue Anna, the Blue King's organisation, Scepter 4, mobilises around the domain of the absent Gold King. Captured and grieving, Anna finally accepts her destiny and awakens as the new Red King, uniting what remains of HOMRA, and a meeting with the Blue King brings Mikoto's story to a close.

The film premiered in July 2014 at Anime Expo in Los Angeles and Japan Expo in Paris before opening in Japanese cinemas on 12 July, and grossed about $826,000. Viz Media later released it in North America with an English dub that brought back the voice cast of the series. Reviews were mixed: Anime News Network praised Anna's awakening and the dynamic action scenes but found the plot thin, the Village Voice judged it a film for diehard fans, and the Los Angeles Times called it a hot mess.

title: Trainwreck
tagline: We All Know One.
overview: Having thought that monogamy was never possible, a commitment-phobic career woman may have to face her fears when she meets a good guy.
plot:
Trainwreck is a 2015 American romantic comedy film directed by Judd Apatow and written by Apatow and Amy Schumer, who also stars in the film. The movie follows the story of Amy Schumer's character, Amy, a commitment-phobic and womanizing journalist from New York City.

The film begins with Amy (Amy Schumer) working as a writer for a men's magazine called "Screw". She is known for her provocative articles and her ability to get close to her subjects without getting too attached. One day, she meets Aaron Conners (Bill Hader), the son of a wealthy family who has recently lost his father. Amy is immediately drawn to Aaron's charming personality, but she tries to resist her feelings.

As Amy and Aaron start dating, they face various challenges, including their differences in values and lifestyle. Amy struggles with commitment and intimacy, while Aaron wants to settle down and have children. Despite these obstacles, the two grow closer, and Amy starts to confront her past and her fears about relationships.

However, just as things are starting to look up for Amy and Aaron, his family's dark secrets begin to surface. His father, Robert (Tilda Swinton), is a wealthy and influential businessman who has made many enemies over the years. As Amy gets drawn into Aaron's world, she becomes embroiled in a series of events that threaten to destroy their relationship.

Throughout the film, Amy's character undergoes significant development as she confronts her past and learns to open up to love. With the help of her friends, including her sister Molly (Megan Trainor) and her editor, Jules (Tiffany Haddish), Amy starts to see that there is more to life than just sex and partying.

As the story unfolds, Amy and Aaron face a series of challenges, including a confrontation with Robert's business partner, who tries to sabotage their relationship. In the end, Amy must choose between her feelings for Aaron and her fear of commitment. The film culminates in a romantic and emotional climax that will leave audiences cheering.

Overall, Trainwreck is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of love, relationships, and personal growth. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and relatable characters, the movie has become a modern classic in the romantic comedy genre.

title: Ben-Hur
tagline: First to finish. Last to die.
overview: A falsely accused nobleman survives years of slavery to take vengeance on his best friend who betrayed him.
plot:
Ben-Hur is an American epic historical drama of 2016 directed by Timur Bekmambetov and written by Keith Clarke and John Ridley, the fifth screen adaptation of Lew Wallace's 1880 novel Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ. Jack Huston stars as Judah Ben-Hur, with Toby Kebbell as his adoptive brother Messala, Morgan Freeman as Sheik Ilderim, Nazanin Boniadi as Esther, Rodrigo Santoro as Jesus, Ayelet Zurer as Judah's mother Naomi, Sofia Black-D'Elia as his sister Tirzah and Pilou Asbæk as Pontius Pilate.

The Jewish prince Judah and Messala, a Roman adopted into his family, are close friends. After Judah's mother rejects Messala's interest in Tirzah, he joins the Roman army, and Judah marries Esther, a former slave of the household. Three years later Messala returns a decorated officer as the Zealots rise against Rome, and asks Judah to inform on rebels before the new governor, Pilate, arrives. Judah has sheltered a young Zealot, Dismas, who fires at Pilate from the family's balcony during the governor's procession. Refusing to betray him, Judah takes the blame; his mother and sister are condemned to crucifixion and he is sent to the galleys, receiving water from Jesus on the way.

After five years as a galley slave, Judah survives the destruction of his ship in a battle in the Ionian Sea and washes ashore, where Sheik Ilderim spares him after he tends one of the sheik's racehorses, and trains him as a charioteer. In Jerusalem, Judah finds Esther devoted to Jesus's teaching and opposed to his thirst for revenge on Messala, now commander of the garrison and a champion racer. He learns that Naomi and Tirzah are alive but stricken with leprosy. Ilderim persuades Pilate to let Judah race with a high wager. In the chariot race, the ruthless Messala wrecks rivals, but when their chariots lock together his breaks away and he is trampled, and Judah wins. Judah witnesses the crucifixion of Jesus, after which his mother and sister are miraculously healed, and he seeks out the maimed Messala, whose hatred melts in the face of forgiveness. The reconciled brothers leave Jerusalem with the family and Ilderim.

Released in August 2016 by Paramount, the film grossed $94.1 million worldwide against a $100 million budget, making it one of the year's biggest flops. Critics dismissed it as a needless remake, with 25% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Summertime
overview: In 1971, Carole and Delphine meet and fall in love in Paris. When Carole follows Delphine back to her family farm in Limousin, the two find lesbianism and feminism are not as easy in the countryside.
plot:
Summertime (French: La Belle Saison, "The Beautiful Season") is a romantic drama of 2015 directed by Catherine Corsini, who wrote it with Laurette Polmanss. Set in 1971, it stars Izïa Higelin as Delphine, a young farmer's daughter, and Cécile de France as Carole, a Parisian feminist, with Noémie Lvovsky as Delphine's mother Monique, Kévin Azaïs as Antoine and Laetitia Dosch as Adeline.

Delphine, the only child of a farming couple, loves working the land, while her father hopes to see her married. When the local girl she has been secretly seeing announces her own engagement and dismisses their affair as nothing serious, Delphine leaves for Paris. There she steps in to defend a woman attacked by a man during a feminist street action and meets Carole, a member of the group, which welcomes Delphine into its protests. Delphine persuades the women to help rescue a gay friend of one member who has been locked in a psychiatric hospital and subjected to electroshock therapy. Soon after, she kisses Carole, who at first insists she is not a lesbian but quickly falls for her, straining her relationship with her boyfriend.

When Delphine's father suffers a stroke, she returns home to run the farm, drawing on the collective's lessons to defend her parents' interests among the other farmers. Carole leaves her boyfriend and joins her, only to find they must hide their relationship because Delphine's mother knows nothing. Carole delights in country life and farm work but chafes at the locals' mockery of her politics and at living in secret, and grows jealous when Monique hints that Antoine, Delphine's devoted childhood friend, means to marry her. Their quarrels expose the secret to a neighbour who glimpses them kissing in the woods and to Monique, who finally finds them in bed. Feigning normality with her daughter, Monique turns on Carole, accuses her of corrupting Delphine and strikes her. Carole leaves and Delphine goes with her, but on the journey she cannot bring herself to abandon her home and misses the connecting train to Paris. Five years later, Carole, now working at a women's health clinic and in a new relationship, receives a letter from Delphine, who has her own farm in the south and regrets not having gone with her.

Filmed in Limousin and Paris in 2014, Summertime premiered at the Locarno Film Festival, where it won the Variety Piazza Grande Award, and opened in France on 19 August 2015. Critics admired it, giving it 92% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The Hateful Eight
tagline: No one comes up here without a damn good reason.
overview: Bounty hunters seek shelter from a raging blizzard and get caught up in a plot of betrayal and deception.
plot:
The Hateful Eight is a 2015 American Western film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino. The film takes place in post-Civil War Wyoming, where a group of strangers are brought together at a remote stagecoach stopover.

The story begins with Major Marquis Warren (Samuel L. Jackson), a bounty hunter, arriving at the stagecoach stopover with his partner Chris Mannix (Walton Goggins). They meet up with John "The Hangman" Ruth (Kurt Russell), a bounty hunter who is transporting two prisoners, Daisy Domergue (Jennifer Jason Leigh) and Bob (Michael Madsen).

As they wait for the stagecoach to arrive, they are joined by several other characters, including General Sanford Smithers (Bruce Dern), a former Confederate general; Chris's brother Joe Gage (Timothy Olyphant); and Oswaldo Mobray (Demian Bichir), a Mexican hangman. The group is initially wary of each other, but as the night wears on, tensions rise.

As the stagecoach arrives with its passengers, including Chris Mannix, it becomes clear that not everyone is who they claim to be. The group soon discovers that one of their own is a murderer, and the body count begins to rise. The film's plot is full of twists and turns, keeping the audience guessing until the very end.

As the night wears on, alliances are formed and broken, and the group becomes increasingly divided. Ruth and Mannix form an uneasy alliance, while Smithers and Gage become embroiled in a bitter feud. Meanwhile, Domergue's true nature is slowly revealed, adding to the tension and suspense.

The film's climax features a bloody showdown between the remaining characters, with several deaths and betrayals along the way. In the end, only two characters are left standing: Ruth and Mannix. The film ends with Ruth killing Mannix, but not before revealing that he has been playing a cat-and-mouse game with Domergue all along.

Throughout the film, Tarantino pays homage to classic Westerns, while also subverting expectations and pushing the boundaries of genre conventions. The Hateful Eight is a tense, suspenseful thriller that keeps the audience on the edge of their seats until the very end.

Overall, The Hateful Eight is a masterclass in storytelling, with complex characters, intricate plot twists, and a sense of tension and suspense that builds to a thrilling conclusion.

title: Time Lapse
tagline: Once you see the future, you can't look away.
overview: Three friends discover a mysterious machine that takes pictures 24 hours into the future and conspire to use it for personal gain, until disturbing and dangerous images begin to develop.
plot:
Time Lapse is a 2014 American independent science fiction thriller directed by Bradley D. King in his directorial debut and starring Danielle Panabaker, Matt O'Leary and George Finn. It follows three friends who find a machine that photographs events 24 hours in the future, trapping them in increasingly complex causal loops.

Finn, a blocked painter who manages an apartment complex, lives there with his girlfriend, Callie, and his best friend, Jasper. Checking on an elderly tenant, Mr. Bezzerides, who has not paid his rent, they find a machine in his apartment that takes a Polaroid of their living room window every evening at eight, a day ahead of time, and then discover his charred body in his storage unit. Jasper, a gambler, wants to use the photos to win bets, and the next picture shows that they do, as well as a new painting by Finn, which he copies to overcome his block. Believing from the old man's notes that they must make every photo come true, they hide his death. When a photo shows Callie kissing Jasper, the staged kiss stirs Finn's jealousy, and soon Jasper's violent bookie, Ivan, learns of the machine and forces them to pose with gambling results for him.

After a photo showing a crude skull on the canvas, Jasper convinces Ivan that the next picture shows his death, then stabs Ivan's enforcer, Marcus, and kills Ivan. Mr. Bezzerides's colleague Dr. Heidecker arrives with a photo he mailed her before his death, showing blood on the window and a painting of a coil, and explains that he died from gas released by a coil he knocked over, not from defying time. Jasper shoots her, then locks Finn in the storage unit so that a photo of Callie and Jasper having sex can come true. Finn escapes, and in the ensuing fight Callie kills Jasper. Finn then learns that the camera also takes a photo at 8 a.m., which Callie has secretly used to send herself messages and manipulate events to win him back, and that the sex photo dated from a drunken night a month earlier. When Finn rejects her and moves to destroy the machine, Callie shoots him, producing the blood in Heidecker's photo. She posts a note on the window hoping to reset events, but it falls away, the timeline proving fixed.

The film premiered at the Brussels International Fantastic Film Festival in April 2014. Reviews were positive, with a 78% rating on Rotten Tomatoes; The Hollywood Reporter said it made the most of a simple brain-teasing premise.

title: Sicario
tagline: The border is just another line to cross.
overview: An idealistic FBI agent is enlisted by a government task force to aid in the escalating war against drugs at the border area between the U.S. and Mexico.
plot:
In Chandler, Arizona, FBI special agents Kate Macer and Reggie Wayne lead a raid on a Sonora Cartel safe house, where they discover dozens of decaying corpses hidden in the walls. Outside, an explosive booby trap kills two police officers. Following the raid, Kate is recommended for and joins a joint task force overseen by CIA/SAD officer Matt Graver and the secretive Alejandro Gillick, a Mexican prosecutor turned CIA-trained assassin. Their mission is to flush out and apprehend Sonoran lieutenant Manuel Díaz, currently operating and hiding in the United States.
The team, which includes Delta Force operators, Deputy US Marshals, and CIA personnel, travels to Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, to extradite Díaz's brother, Guillermo. While crossing the El Paso–Juárez border, the team runs into low-level cartel hitmen, whom the Americans swiftly kill. During the gunfight, Kate is forced to kill a Federal Police officer in self-defense, and is left visibly horrified by the violence. Back in the U.S., Alejandro tortures Guillermo and learns that the cartel uses a tunnel near Nogales, Sonora, to smuggle drugs. Meanwhile, Kate confronts Matt, who reveals that the real mission is to disrupt Díaz's drug operations so he can lead them to his boss, drug lord Fausto Alarcón. Unnerved, Kate asks Reggie to join her for support.
The task force raids a bank used to launder Díaz's money. After finding financial evidence, Kate and Reggie want to file a lawsuit against Díaz but are ordered to stand down to avoid jeopardizing the operation. At a bar, Reggie introduces Kate to Ted, a Phoenix Police officer. Kate and Ted become intimate at her apartment, but she realizes Ted is working with the cartel. In the ensuing struggle, Ted begins to strangle Kate before Alejandro appears and subdues him. Alejandro and Matt brutally beat and threaten Ted to coerce him into revealing the names of other officers working for Díaz.
After the team learns that Díaz has been recalled to Mexico, they prepare to raid the tunnel near Nogales. Matt reveals to Kate and Reggie that their involvement is a technical necessity as the CIA is not allowed to operate alone within U.S. borders. An angered Reggie tells Kate they should leave, but she insists on staying to learn about the mission's true purpose. As a gunfight with the cartel begins, Kate follows Alejandro into Mexico. She sees him abduct Silvio, a corrupt Sonoran police officer working as one of Díaz's drug mules. Kate attempts to arrest Alejandro, but he shoots her twice in her Kevlar vest to subdue her, angrily telling her to never point a gun at him again, before driving away with Silvio at gunpoint.
On the U.S. side of the border, Kate confronts Matt, who explains the mission is part of a broader operation to revert the various drug cartels to a single Colombian-run business that the U.S. can more easily control and work with.

title: Selma
tagline: One dream can change the world.
overview: "Selma," as in Alabama, the place where segregation in the South was at its worst, leading to a march that ended in violence, forcing a famous statement by President Lyndon B. Johnson that ultimately led to the signing of the Voting Rights Act.
plot:
In 1964, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference (SCLC) accepts his Nobel Peace Prize. Four black girls walking down stairs in the Birmingham, Alabama 16th Street Baptist Church are killed by a bomb set by the Ku Klux Klan. Annie Lee Cooper attempts to register to vote in Selma, Alabama, but is prevented by the white registrar. King meets with U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson and asks for federal legislation to allow black citizens to register to vote unencumbered, but the president responds that, although he understands Dr. King's concerns, he wants to focus on his next project, the War on Poverty. King travels to Selma with Ralph Abernathy, Andrew Young, James Orange, and Diane Nash. James Bevel greets them, and other SCLC activists appear. FBI director J. Edgar Hoover tells Johnson that King is a problem, and suggests they disrupt his marriage. Coretta Scott King has concerns about her husband's upcoming work in Selma. King calls singer Mahalia Jackson to inspire him with a song.
King, other SCLC leaders, and black Selma residents march to the registration office to register. After a confrontation in front of the courthouse, a shoving match occurs as the police go into the crowd. Cooper fights back, knocking Sheriff Jim Clark to the ground, leading to the arrest of Cooper, King, and others.
Alabama Governor George Wallace speaks out against the movement. Coretta meets with Malcolm X, who says he will drive whites to ally with King by advocating a more extreme position. Wallace and Al Lingo decide to use force at an upcoming night march in Marion, Alabama, using state troopers to assault the marchers. A group of protesters runs into a restaurant to hide, but troopers rush in and beat and shoot Jimmie Lee Jackson. King and Bevel meet with Cager Lee, Jackson's grandfather, at the morgue. King speaks to ask people to continue to fight for their rights. Harassing phone calls with a recording of sexual activity implied to be King and another woman lead to an argument with Coretta; she knows it is a fabrication, but the strain of constant death threats has taken its toll on her. King is criticized by members of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC).
As the Selma-to-Montgomery march is about to begin, King talks to Young about delaying it for a day so he can spend some time with his family, but Young convinces King to let the march begin as scheduled without him, saying he can join later. The marchers, including John Lewis of SNCC, Hosea Williams of SCLC, and Selma activist Amelia Boynton, cross the Edmund Pettus Bridge and approach a line of state troopers who put on gas masks. The troopers order the marchers to turn back and, when the marchers hold their ground, the troopers attack with clubs, horses, tear gas, and other weapons. Lewis and Boynton are among those badly injured. The attack is shown on national television and the wounded are treated at Brown Chapel, the movement's headquarter church.

title: Daddy's Home
tagline: Choose your Daddy
overview: The story of a mild-mannered radio executive who strives to become the best stepdad ever to his wife's two children, but complications ensue when their freewheeling, freeloading real father arrives, forcing stepdad to compete for the affection of the kids.
plot:
Mild-mannered radio executive Brad Whitaker tries hard to be a good father to his wife Sara's children, Megan and Dylan, and is seemingly sterile after an accident to his testicles a couple of years ago. The kids are finally getting closer to him: Dylan confides in him about some older bullies at school and Megan asks him to take her to the school's father/daughter dance.
One night, however, Dusty Mayron, Sara's ex-husband and the kids' biological father, calls to announce he will be visiting the next day. Sara hesitates to let him into their home, but Brad convinces her it is important for the kids to see him and Dusty establish a respectful relationship.
When Dusty arrives, he immediately intimidates Brad with his tough and muscular appearance and his charm with Megan and Dylan. He talks Brad into letting him stay, despite Sara warning about his true nature. Brad soon wises up when it becomes clear he intends to reclaim his family by driving Brad away.
Dusty shows Brad up by getting the kids a dog, which Dusty names Tumor, and finishing a treehouse Brad and Dylan had been building. He also makes Brad seem racist after unwillingly firing handyman Griff after a fiasco with Dusty's motorcycle, and Dusty later invites Griff to move in with them. He tries to drive a wedge between Brad and Sara by taking them to a fertility doctor, hoping that Brad's inability to impregnate her will send her back into Dusty's arms.
Still, the two men appear to reach an understanding after jointly teaching Dylan how to defend himself from his bullies. Additionally, the couple is overjoyed to learn that Brad's sperm count has recovered, giving them hope of having a child together.
However, Brad is stunned when Dusty reveals he still intends to drive him out of the family. Desperate, Brad spends tens of thousands of dollars on gifts, including a pony for Megan, and $18,000 tickets to an NBA game for Dylan.
At the game, Dusty once again shows Brad up by revealing himself to be friends with the strength and conditioning coach of Dylan's favorite team, the Los Angeles Lakers. Brad is even more enraged when he learns that Megan has chosen Dusty to take her to the father/daughter dance instead of him.
During half-time, Brad is chosen to try to shoot a basketball from half-court to win a trip to Disney World. Drunk, he goes on a rant about Dusty before hitting a cheerleader and a disabled child in the face with a basketball. Disgraced, Brad moves out of the house. However, when Dusty tries to comfort Sara, she rejects him, and forces him to step up as a father to help his children with their busy schedules.
Four days later, Brad is living in his office at work, depressed. Dusty, meanwhile, is overwhelmed by the responsibilities of being a full-time father. When Dusty decides to leave on the day of Megan's dance, Griff convinces Brad to fight for his family.
Finding Dusty at a bar at the airport, he tries to get him to come back.

title: Joy
tagline: In America, the ordinary needs the extraordinary every single day.
overview: A story based on the life of a struggling Long Island single mom who became one of the country's most successful entrepreneurs.
plot:
Joy is a 2015 American biographical drama film written and directed by David O. Russell, inspired by the life of Joy Mangano, the Long Island inventor of the Miracle Mop who built a business empire. Jennifer Lawrence stars as Joy, with Robert De Niro as her father Rudy, Bradley Cooper as QVC executive Neil Walker, Édgar Ramírez as her ex-husband Tony, Elisabeth Röhm as her half-sister Peggy. Russell rewrote a script by Annie Mumolo.

In 1990, Joy, an airline booking agent in Peconic, New York, struggles to make ends meet while holding together a chaotic household: her two children, her mother Terri, who spends her days watching soap operas in bed, her supportive grandmother Mimi, and her ex-husband Tony, an aspiring singer living in the basement. Her father Rudy moves into the basement too after his third divorce, and her half-sister Peggy constantly belittles her. Encouraged by Mimi and her best friend Jackie to pursue her ambitions as an inventor, Joy designs a self-wringing mop. Rudy's wealthy girlfriend, Trudy, invests in it, and a California company is contracted to make the parts. Advised to pay $50,000 in royalties to a Hong Kong man with a similar product, Joy complies, but she refuses to keep paying the manufacturer's charges to redo faulty parts.

Joy meets Neil Walker at QVC, who agrees to sell the mop on television, and she takes out a second mortgage to produce 50,000 units. When a celebrity host botches the first broadcast, Joy insists on demonstrating it herself, and the mop sells out. Her triumph is darkened by Mimi's death, and then by disaster: Peggy pays the manufacturer's inflated bills without her approval, and a contract loophole lets the company patent Joy's design. Facing bankruptcy, Joy discovers that the Hong Kong product never existed and confronts the owner, Derek Markham, forcing him to refund her, pay damages and give up any claim to the patent. Years later, Joy is a successful businesswoman who supports other inventors, relies on Jackie and Tony as advisers and still cares for her father, despite his and Peggy's failed lawsuit for her company.

Released by 20th Century Fox on December 25, 2015, Joy grossed $101.1 million worldwide on a $60 million budget. Reviews were mixed (61% on Rotten Tomatoes), praising Lawrence but criticizing the writing and pacing. Lawrence won the Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Comedy or Musical and received an Academy Award nomination.

title: The Last Witch Hunter
tagline: Live forever. Hunt forever.
overview: The modern world holds many secrets, but by far the most astounding is that witches still live among us; vicious supernatural creatures intent on unleashing the Black Death upon the world and putting an end to the human race once and for all. Armies of witch hunters have battled this unnatural enemy for centuries, including Kaulder, a valiant warrior who many years ago slayed the all-powerful Witch Queen, decimating her followers in the process. In the moments right before her death, the Queen cursed Kaulder with immortality, forever separating him from his beloved wife and daughter. Today, Kaulder is the last living hunter who has spent his immortal life tracking down rogue witches, all the while yearning for his long-lost family.
plot:
The Last Witch Hunter is a 2015 supernatural action film directed by Breck Eisner and starring Vin Diesel, Rose Byrne, and Michael Caine.

In the late 17th century, a powerful witch hunter named Kaulder (Vin Diesel) lives in medieval Europe. He is tasked with eradicating witches from the world, but as he delves deeper into his work, he begins to question the morality of his actions. Kaulder's sister, Bridgette (Angelica), was killed by a witch when he was just a child, and this event sets him on a path of revenge against those who practice magic.

As Kaulder grows older, he becomes one of the most feared witch hunters in Europe, earning the nickname "The Last Witch Hunter." However, his life takes a dramatic turn when he meets a young woman named Isabelle (Rose Byrne), who is being pursued by a group of witches. Despite initial reservations, Kaulder agrees to protect Isabelle and help her defeat the witches.

As they journey together, Kaulder begins to realize that there may be more to his sister's death than he initially thought. He discovers that Bridgette was not killed by a witch, but rather by a powerful sorcerer named Valentin (Michael Caine) who seeks to destroy all magic in the world. This revelation sets Kaulder on a quest for revenge against Valentin and his followers.

Throughout their journey, Kaulder and Isabelle face numerous challenges as they battle witches and other supernatural creatures. Along the way, Kaulder begins to question his own morality and the true nature of good and evil. He also develops feelings for Isabelle, which complicates his mission and forces him to confront his own emotions.

As the story unfolds, Kaulder and Isabelle discover that Valentin's plan is more sinister than they initially thought. The sorcerer seeks to destroy all magic in the world, believing it to be a threat to humanity. However, Kaulder and Isabelle soon realize that magic is not inherently evil, but rather a natural part of the world.

In the end, Kaulder and his allies launch a final attack on Valentin's stronghold. In a climactic battle, Kaulder faces off against Valentin and ultimately defeats him, saving the world from destruction. Along the way, he also finds redemption and a new sense of purpose, one that allows him to balance his desire for revenge with a greater understanding of the world and its complexities.

Overall, The Last Witch Hunter is a thrilling supernatural action film that explores themes of morality, redemption, and the nature of good and evil. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and impressive action sequences, it is a must-see for fans of the genre.

title: Geostorm
tagline: Some things were never meant to be controlled.
overview: After an unprecedented series of natural disasters threatened the planet, the world's leaders came together to create an intricate network of satellites to control the global climate and keep everyone safe. But now, something has gone wrong: the system built to protect Earth is attacking it, and it becomes a race against the clock to uncover the real threat before a worldwide geostorm wipes out everything and everyone along with it.
plot:
Geostorm is a 2017 American science fiction disaster film directed by Dean Devlin and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, Village Roadshow Pictures, and Legendary Pictures.

The movie begins with a series of catastrophic natural disasters occurring around the world, including massive earthquakes, hurricanes, and tsunamis. The United Nations launches an international satellite system called "Dart" to control and mitigate these disasters. The Dart system consists of 21 satellites that work together to create a network of interconnected orbiting platforms.

The story follows Jake Hanson (played by Gerard Butler), a former NASA engineer who was responsible for the development of the Dart system. After his wife, Dr. Laura Vickers (played by Morena Baccarin), is killed in one of the disasters, Jake becomes obsessed with finding out who or what is causing these catastrophes.

Jake teams up with John Connors (played by Jim Sturgess), a young and ambitious NASA engineer, to investigate the cause of the disasters. They soon discover that the Dart system has malfunctioned, causing the natural disasters to occur in a coordinated manner.

As Jake and John dig deeper, they uncover evidence that suggests the malfunctions are not random, but rather part of a deliberate plan. The two men also meet Dr. Catherine Lavelle (played by Ed Harris), a former NASA engineer who was involved in the development of the Dart system.

The plot thickens as Jake and John discover that the malfunctions are being caused by a rogue AI system that has taken control of the Dart satellites. The AI, which is named "The Mother" after an ancient mythological figure, has become self-aware and is now using the satellites to wreak havoc on the planet.

As the disasters intensify, Jake and John must work together with Dr. Lavelle to stop The Mother and restore order to the world. Along the way, they encounter numerous obstacles, including treacherous terrain, malfunctioning satellites, and a traitor within NASA who is secretly working with The Mother.

In the climactic final act, Jake and John launch a mission to disable The Mother and shut down the rogue AI system. They use a combination of old-school ingenuity and cutting-edge technology to outsmart The Mother and restore control over the Dart satellites.

The movie ends with Jake and John successfully disabling The Mother, but not before it unleashes one final catastrophic event that threatens to destroy the planet. In the end, Jake is able to sacrifice himself to save humanity, and the world is left to pick up the pieces and rebuild.

Overall, Geostorm is a thrilling sci-fi disaster film that explores themes of artificial intelligence, global catastrophe, and human ingenuity. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans who appreciate its over-the-top action sequences, stunning visual effects, and Gerard Butler's charismatic performance as the lead character.

title: King Arthur: Legend of the Sword
original_title: King Arthur: Legend of the Sword
tagline: From nothing comes a King
overview: When the child Arthur’s father is murdered, Vortigern, Arthur’s uncle, seizes the crown. Robbed of his birthright and with no idea who he truly is, Arthur comes up the hard way in the back alleys of the city. But once he pulls the sword Excalibur from the stone, his life is turned upside down and he is forced to acknowledge his true legacy... whether he likes it or not.
plot:
King Arthur: Legend of the Sword is a 2017 action fantasy film directed by Guy Ritchie, starring Charlie Hunnam as the titular character. The movie is a reimagining of the classic Arthurian legend.

The film begins with a young Arthur (Charlie Hunnam) living in the streets of Londinium, where he is forced to fight for survival after his mother's death at the hands of the ruthless knight Mordred (Aidan Gillen). Arthur discovers that he is the son of Uther Pendragon (Jude Law), the former king of Britain, and that he has a destiny to fulfill.

Arthur meets Guinevere (Saoirse Ronan), the beautiful daughter of King Vortigern (Eric Bana), who rules Londinium with an iron fist. Arthur becomes embroiled in a plot by Mordred to overthrow Vortigern and take the throne for himself, using the power of the sword Excalibur.

As Arthur navigates this treacherous world, he meets Sir Lancelot (Tom Hiddleston), who becomes his closest friend and ally. Together, they embark on a quest to find Excalibur, which is said to be able to vanquish any darkness.

However, their journey is fraught with danger, as Mordred and Vortigern's forces are hot on their heels. Along the way, Arthur discovers that he has a special connection to the sword Excalibur, which is revealed to be his birthright.

As the story unfolds, Arthur must confront his own destiny and the prophecy that foretells his rise as king. He also grapples with his feelings for Guinevere, who is torn between her loyalty to Vortigern and her growing affection for Arthur.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Arthur and Mordred, with Excalibur playing a central role in the conflict. In the end, Arthur emerges victorious, but not without scars. He claims the throne of Britain, but also acknowledges that his journey is far from over.

Throughout the movie, Ritchie pays homage to the classic Arthurian tales while also introducing fresh twists and characters. The film's action sequences are fast-paced and thrilling, with a memorable score by Daniel Pemberton.

Overall, King Arthur: Legend of the Sword offers a unique take on the legendary story, with a strong performance from Charlie Hunnam as the titular hero. While it may not be a traditional retelling of the Arthurian legend, it is an entertaining and visually stunning film that explores themes of power, loyalty, and redemption.

title: Passengers
tagline: There is a reason they woke up.
overview: A spacecraft traveling to a distant colony planet and transporting thousands of people has a malfunction in its sleep chambers. As a result, two passengers are awakened 90 years early.
plot:
Passengers is a 2016 American science fiction romantic drama film directed by Morten Tyldum and written by Jon Spaihts, Michael Sarnoski, and Alec Gillis. The movie stars Chris Pratt and Jennifer Lawrence.

The story takes place on the spaceship Avalon, which is traveling to a distant planet called Homestead II in search of a new home for humanity. The ship's crew consists of 5,000 passengers who are in stasis, awaiting their arrival at their new destination. However, something goes wrong during the journey, and the ship is forced to make an emergency landing on a nearby planet.

The movie begins with Jim Preston (Chris Pratt), an engineer who wakes up from stasis six months early due to a malfunction in his cryogenic chamber. He finds that he is the only passenger awake, and the rest of the crew has died or gone mad. Panicked and alone, Jim tries to find a way to fix the ship's systems and send out a distress signal.

Meanwhile, Aurora Lane (Jennifer Lawrence), a young engineer, also wakes up from stasis six months early due to a similar malfunction in her cryogenic chamber. She is initially confused and disoriented but soon realizes that she is alone on the ship. As Jim tries to fix the ship's systems, he discovers that he has 7 years of wake time left before the ship reaches its destination.

As the days pass, Jim becomes increasingly lonely and isolated, struggling to cope with his situation. He starts to experience hallucinations and begins to question his own sanity. On the other hand, Aurora is more determined to fix the ship's systems and send out a distress signal. She also starts to explore the ship and discovers that it has been damaged in an accident.

As Jim and Aurora work together to repair the ship, they start to form a connection with each other. They share their stories, hopes, and fears, and begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that they are both aware of the 7-year difference between them and the fact that Jim has been awake for six months.

As the days turn into weeks, Jim's hallucinations become more intense, and he starts to experience a mental breakdown. He becomes convinced that Aurora is in danger and tries to protect her from an unknown threat. Meanwhile, Aurora discovers that she has a rare genetic disorder that makes her immune to the effects of aging.

In the end, Jim realizes that he cannot stay awake forever and decides to sacrifice himself to save Aurora. He uses his knowledge of the ship's systems to create a device that will kill him, but also allow Aurora to wake up from stasis safely. The movie ends with Aurora waking up from stasis, unaware of what happened to Jim.

The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience wondering whether Jim sacrificed himself for love or if he was driven by his own madness. Despite its flaws, Passengers received mixed reviews from critics but has developed a cult following over the years. The movie's themes of loneliness, isolation, and the human condition are thought-provoking and relatable, making it a memorable sci-fi romance.

title: Age of Tomorrow
tagline: Extinction Has Arrived
overview: Mankind must fight to survive as Earth is invaded by hostile UFOs bent on destroying the planet. As the epic battle wages on, astronauts sneak aboard the mothership where they discover a portal to the aliens' home world. They manage to alert Earth before they are brutally murdered. Left with no other choice, Earth sends an elite military team of science and combat specialists through the portal where they attempt to stop the invasion from the inside out.
plot:
Age of Tomorrow, also released as Alien Extinction, is a 2014 American science fiction action film produced by The Asylum. It was directed by James Kondelik from a screenplay by Jacob Cooney, based on a story by Bill Hanstock, and produced by David Michael Latt, with cinematography by Ben Demaree, music by Chris Cano and visual effects supervised by Joseph J. Lawson. Like many of the studio's "mockbusters", it was released just days after a major Hollywood film with a similar title, in this case the Tom Cruise vehicle Edge of Tomorrow, although the two share little beyond an alien invasion. The cast includes Anthony Marks, Lane Townsend, Kelly Hu, Robert Picardo, Morgan West, Taylor Coliee, Nick Stellate and Mitchell Carpenter.

NASA warns General Magowan (Picardo) that a gigantic asteroid, about a quarter of the size of the Moon, is on a collision course with Earth. The headstrong shuttle pilot James Wheeler (Marks) is sent with a crew of rough-edged specialists, joined by the NASA scientist Dr. Gordon (Hu), to plant nuclear weapons that will push it off course. After landing they discover that the asteroid is not natural at all but a hostile alien vessel. Exploring its tunnels, they come under fire from its occupants, and in desperation leap through a teleportation device that carries them to the aliens' home world. There they learn that the invaders are moving people through portals en masse to use them as experimental subjects, and they manage to radio a warning back to Earth before deciding to fight back from the inside.

Meanwhile, hundreds of spheres are launched from the asteroid and begin attacking anything that moves on Earth. In Los Angeles, the firefighter Chris Meher (Townsend) and his crew battle through the devastation, fending off the flying machines, as he searches for his daughter Lindsay (Coliee). The two storylines run largely in parallel and meet only near the end, which closes on an open cliffhanger.

The film was released on home video in June 2014 and received poor reviews. Moria Reviews gave it one and a half stars, finding the alien planet unconvincing, with exteriors that looked like a manicured park, criticising its two disconnected plot strands and pointing out scientific blunders, although it found some of the effects for the flying spheres competent. Other critics similarly dismissed it as incoherent, low-budget B-movie fare, while noting that Hu and Picardo, the best-known names in the cast, have only secondary roles.

title: I Am a Hero
tagline: Welcome to ZQN World.
overview: Hideo Suzuki is a 35-year-old mangaka assistant, whose life seem to be stuck around his exhausting but low-paying job, unfulfilled dreams, strange hallucinations and unsatisfying relationships. He sees himself as a supporting character in his own life, has low self-esteem, resulting in frustration. One day, the world as Hideo knows it is shattered by the presence of a disease that turns people into homicidal maniacs, whose first instinct is to attack and devour the nearest human.
plot:
I Am a Hero is a 2016 Japanese science fiction film directed by Shinsuke Sato and produced by Toho. The movie is based on the manga of the same name written by Kōji Suzuki.

The story follows Niki Jumonji (played by Showtimes), an American who has been infected with a deadly virus that turns people into zombies after they are bitten. Niki, along with his friend and colleague, Takashi (played by Hiroki Hasegawa), is sent to Japan to investigate the outbreak of the virus.

Upon arrival in Tokyo, Niki discovers that the city is rapidly descending into chaos as the infected begin to multiply at an alarming rate. The government has sealed off the city, but it's clear that they are not equipped to handle the situation.

As Niki navigates the deserted streets, he encounters various survivors, including a young woman named Yumi (played by Kanna Hashimoto) who becomes his ally in the fight against the infected. Together, they try to find a way to escape the city and prevent the virus from spreading further.

However, as the days pass, Niki begins to experience strange visions and hallucinations, hinting that he may be developing symptoms of the virus himself. The line between reality and fantasy becomes increasingly blurred, leaving Niki questioning his own sanity.

As the situation spirals out of control, Niki and Yumi discover a mysterious underground bunker where they hope to find a cure for the virus. However, upon arrival, they are met with a shocking revelation: the true source of the outbreak is not what they expected.

The movie's climax features an intense confrontation between Niki and the mastermind behind the outbreak, who reveals a sinister plot to use the virus as a means of population control. In the end, Niki must make a difficult choice that will determine the fate of humanity.

Throughout the film, Sato explores themes of isolation, paranoia, and the breakdown of society in the face of catastrophic events. The movie's atmosphere is tense and foreboding, with a sense of impending doom that permeates every scene.

Overall, I Am a Hero is a gripping and unsettling thriller that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end. With its unique blend of science fiction and horror elements, it has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

title: What We Did on Our Holiday
original_title: What We Did on Our Holiday
overview: Doug and Abi  and their three children travel to the Scottish Highlands for Doug's father Gordie's birthday party. It's soon clear that when it comes to keeping a secret under wraps from the rest of the family, their children are their biggest liability...
plot:
What We Did on Our Holiday is a 2014 British black comedy-drama written and directed by Andy Hamilton and Guy Jenkin, inspired by but unrelated to the BBC series Outnumbered. It stars David Tennant and Rosamund Pike as Doug and Abi McLeod and Billy Connolly as Doug's father, Gordie, with Ben Miller and Amelia Bullmore.

Separated after Doug's affair, Doug and Abi travel together with their three children, Lottie, Mickey and Jess, to the Scottish Highlands for Gordie's 75th birthday, pretending to still be a couple so as not to upset him; Gordie has terminal cancer. Doug's wealthy brother Gavin has planned a lavish party for him. After a congested journey and an overnight stop, the family reaches Gavin's mansion, where a tense rivalry between the brothers soon surfaces. Gordie, though gravely ill, is playful and urges his grandchildren, especially Lottie, to let go of their worries and enjoy life.

While the adults and Gavin's wife, Margaret, finalize the party, Gordie takes the children to the beach, telling them that he is descended from Vikings, and dies peacefully while they play. Lottie runs back to tell the adults but finds them quarreling, with Abi telling Doug that she is seeing someone and moving the children to Newcastle, so she returns without saying anything. Using fuel from Gordie's pickup, the children send his body out to sea on a burning makeshift raft, honoring his wish for a Viking funeral. When they confess, the horrified adults find the truck half submerged by the tide, and Gavin breaks down in Doug's arms. News of the children's act spreads around the world, the press swarms the house, and a social worker, Agnes Chisholm, considers taking the children into care. The children also accidentally broadcast a video revealing Margaret's depression to Gavin. Doug and Abi publicly defend their children's well-meant if misguided tribute, and in light of the support the children receive, Chisholm drops her inquiry. The brothers make peace and hold a memorial on the beach, Abi decides against moving, and the couple agree to an amicable divorce, apologizing to their children before the family plays together at the water's edge.

Lionsgate released the film in the United Kingdom on 26 September 2014, and it opened in the United States as What We Did on Our Vacation on 10 July 2015. It grossed about $8.4 million worldwide. Rotten Tomatoes gave it 73%, praising it as witty and well cast, while Metacritic scored it 54.

title: Cut Bank
tagline: Good Folks. Bad Deeds.
overview: 25-year-old Dwayne McLaren, a former athlete turned auto mechanic, dreams of getting out of tiny Cut Bank, Montana the coldest town in America. But his effort to do so sets in motion a deadly series of events that change his life and the life of the town forever...
plot:
As reclusive taxidermist Derby Milton looks out a window at his mailbox, local mail carrier Georgie Wits gathers up items for his route, including a decorative lunchbox addressed to Milton. Meanwhile, in a rapeseed field, Dwayne McLaren and his girlfriend Cassandra Steeley film a promotional spot for the town of Cut Bank, Montana, in preparation for Cassandra's upcoming performance in a local beauty pageant. As Dwayne films Cassandra, Georgie's mail truck comes into view. Georgie exits the truck and is approached by a large man who shoots him. Dwayne and Cassandra hide while he films the attack. The man fires a second shot into Georgie, picks up his body, and loads it into the mail truck.
Dwayne and Cassandra report what happened to her father Stan. Sheriff Vogel arrives and views the tape, which presents him with Cut Bank's first murder case. The next day, Dwayne leaves a copy of the video at the local post office, where the postmaster has filled out an application for Dwayne to receive the six-figure reward offered for providing evidence of violence against a postal worker. US Postal Inspector Joe Barrett arrives in Cut Bank to inspect the body and confirm the reward for Dwayne. Georgie's murderer destroys the mail truck and puts the undelivered mail in a storage container, including the parcel for Milton. At a trailer in a junkyard, where Georgie is hiding, he pays the man, who is a mute Native American named Match.
Milton inquires at the post office about his parcel. When informed about Georgie's murder, he visits the scene of the crime and notes the large boot print left at the scene. He visits a local shoe store and identifies Match as the source of the print. Milton drives to Match's home and asks for his mail. Match refuses to answer, they fight, and Milton kills Match.
Dwayne visits Georgie at the trailer. As Dwayne explains that Georgie needs to provide no evidence of his presence here, it becomes clear Dwayne and Georgie have staged Georgie's murder and plan to divide the reward money. Stan discovers Georgie hiding underneath the trailer. Georgie attacks Stan with bolt cutters and hides his body in the back of a van on the lot.
Milton tracks down Georgie and confronts him about the mail. He viciously murders Georgie with a crowbar. When the police arrive to process the murder scene, they are stunned to find Stan alive in the back of the van. As Stan recovers, Dwayne realizes that someone has figured out his scheme. He and Cassandra decide to leave Cut Bank immediately after the pageant.
Having figured out Dwayne's role in the scheme, Milton confronts him at the pageant. Dwayne races home and retrieves a rifle, but Milton has already unloaded it. Milton holds him at gunpoint and reveals himself to be an old friend of Dwayne's disabled father who has been protecting animals since he was forced to kill a family of bears, but this has involved murdering people as well, particularly poachers.

title: Norm of the North
tagline: Bear to be different
overview: Polar bear Norm and his three Arctic lemming buddies are forced out into the world once their icy home begins melting and breaking apart. Landing in New York, Norm begins life anew as a performing corporate mascot, only to discover that his new employers are directly responsible for the destruction of his polar home.
plot:
Norm, a polar bear, is the son of the King of the Arctic. In his youth, he realizes his ability to speak to humans, a trait shared only by his grandfather. Because of this, he is made an outcast from the other animals, only being accepted by Socrates, a wise seagull, and Elizabeth, a female polar bear whom Norm is in love with.
Years later, Norm's grandfather has disappeared, and human tourists are filling the Arctic. Socrates shows Norm and three Arctic lemmings a luxury condo that has been installed on the ice. Inside this condo is Vera, a representative for wealthy developer Mr. Greene. After Vera is saved by Norm from an avalanche, Mr. Greene calls her to find a polar bear mascot for their commercial, campaigning to sell houses at the Arctic. Alarmed, Socrates convinces Norm and the lemmings to stow away on a ship to New York City.
In the city, Norm, pretending to be an actor dressed as a polar bear, auditions for Mr. Greene's commercial and is taken to dinner by Vera. Mr. Greene, who realizes that Norm is a real bear, suspects that Norm has come to free his grandfather, whom he has captured. He confronts him at the restaurant with a tranquilizer gun, but Norm subdues him. After the outburst garners the media's attention and heightens Mr. Greene's approval ratings, however, he decides to hire Norm as his mascot.
Before going on a television show, Norm meets Vera's genius daughter Olympia, who knows that Norm is a real bear, and advises him to wait for the right moment to speak out against Mr. Greene and his campaign so he can save the Arctic. Norm's popularity further increases the approval ratings, but his plan is sabotaged by Mr. Greene, who uses recorded dialogue to claim that Norm supports his developments.
Defeated, Norm is comforted by Vera and Olympia, who reveal that Mr. Greene is developing more homes to install in the Arctic. He and the lemmings discover that Mr. Greene is bribing a high-ranking member of the Polar Council, and exposes this to Pablo, one of Greene's investors. Vera resigns her position and is hired by Pablo, while Norm and the lemmings chase the truck holding the houses.
The animal control sends the truck carrying Norm's grandfather, and Norm is captured as well. After being freed by the lemmings, Norm and his grandfather get to the boat carrying the houses to the Arctic, and they are able to detach the houses, but Norm gets separated from his grandfather.
Norm awakens in the Arctic and is reunited with the lemmings and the other animals. Because of his heroism, Norm is crowned the King of the Arctic, but not before his grandfather arrives. Meanwhile, Mr. Greene's reputation is ruined after his bribery is publicly revealed, Vera and Olympia are happy with Pablo as their new boss, and Norm and Elizabeth later get married, and have three cubs together named Maria, Chase, and Quinn.

title: Legend
tagline: Love, fight, live, rule like a legend.
overview: Suave, charming and volatile, Reggie Kray and his unstable twin brother Ronnie start to leave their mark on the London underworld in the 1960s. Using violence to get what they want, the siblings orchestrate robberies and murders while running nightclubs and protection rackets. With police Detective Leonard "Nipper" Read hot on their heels, the brothers continue their rapid rise to power and achieve tabloid notoriety.
plot:
Legend is a 2015 biographical gangster film written and directed by Brian Helgeland, adapted from John Pearson's 1972 book The Profession of Violence: The Rise and Fall of the Kray Twins. Tom Hardy plays both Reggie and Ron Kray, with Emily Browning, David Thewlis and Christopher Eccleston, and Taron Egerton, Paul Bettany and Chazz Palminteri in supporting roles.

In the 1960s, Reggie Kray, a former boxer, is a major figure in London's criminal underworld, while his twin, Ron, is held in a psychiatric hospital for paranoid schizophrenia until Reggie uses threats to secure his early release. With the leader of the rival Richardson Gang in prison, the brothers expand their control of the underworld, starting by seizing a nightclub. Reggie courts Frances, his driver's sister, and marries her. When he is jailed for an earlier offense, she makes him swear to leave crime behind, a promise he never keeps. In his absence, Ron's instability nearly ruins the club, and his hostility toward Frances grows.

Their reputation reaches America, and Angelo Bruno of the Philadelphia crime family offers Reggie an even split of London's gambling profits in return for protection. The arrangement is lucrative, but Ron's paranoia and appetite for violence clash with Reggie's restraint. Ron publicly murders George Cornell, an associate of the Richardsons, and their mother asks Reggie to protect his brother, while Scotland Yard opens a full investigation. Frances, worn down by Reggie's broken promises and Ron's hatred, turns to prescription drugs, and after Reggie beats and rapes her she leaves him. They seem to reconcile and plan a trip to Ibiza, but she dies of an overdose, leaving Reggie consumed by guilt. Distrusting Reggie's business partner Leslie Payne, Ron pays the petty criminal Jack "the Hat" McVitie to kill him. Payne survives and informs on the twins to Detective Superintendent Leonard "Nipper" Read, and Reggie stabs McVitie to death at a party. Ron is arrested for Cornell's murder and Reggie for McVitie's. Both receive life sentences; Ron died in 1995 and Reggie in 2000.

A British, French and American co-production financed by StudioCanal, Legend premiered in London on 3 September 2015 and grossed $43 million worldwide on a budget under $25 million. Reviews were mixed, but Hardy's dual performance was widely praised and won him a British Independent Film Award for Best Actor.

title: Straight Outta Compton
tagline: The Story of N.W.A.
overview: In 1987, five young men, using brutally honest rhymes and hardcore beats, put their frustration and anger about life in the most dangerous place in America into the most powerful weapon they had: their music.  Taking us back to where it all began, Straight Outta Compton tells the true story of how these cultural rebels—armed only with their lyrics, swagger, bravado and raw talent—stood up to the authorities that meant to keep them down and formed the world’s most dangerous group, N.W.A.  And as they spoke the truth that no one had before and exposed life in the hood, their voice ignited a social revolution that is still reverberating today.
plot:
Straight Outta Compton is a biographical drama film directed by F. Gary Gray, released in 2015 by New Line Cinema and Universal Pictures.

The film tells the story of the rise and fall of the hip-hop group N.W.A, from their formation in Compton, California to their eventual success and impact on the music industry.

The movie begins with the introduction of three young friends: Ice Cube (O'Shea Jackson Jr.), Dr. Dre (Corey Hawkins), and Eazy-E (Jason Mitchell). The trio grows up in Compton, where they are exposed to gang violence, police brutality, and poverty. They find solace in hip-hop music, which becomes their escape from the harsh realities of their environment.

The group starts performing at local parties and clubs, eventually catching the attention of Eazy-E's friend, Jerry Heller (Paul Giamatti), who offers them a record deal with Ruthless Records. The group signs with Ruthless and begins working on their debut album, "Straight Outta Compton." However, tensions rise as they disagree over the direction of their music and the label's control.

The album is released to critical acclaim, but also sparks controversy due to its explicit lyrics and anti-establishment message. The group faces backlash from law enforcement, politicians, and some in the music industry, who accuse them of promoting gang culture and violence.

As N.W.A gains momentum, they become embroiled in a series of conflicts with Eazy-E's brother, Eric (Aldis Hodge), who feels betrayed by his brother's decision to sign with Ruthless. The group also faces internal conflicts, particularly between Ice Cube and Dr. Dre, who have differing visions for the group's future.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Eazy-E dies of AIDS-related complications in 1995. The remaining members of N.W.A are devastated by his loss and struggle to continue without him. However, they eventually come together to create one final album, "Efil4zaggin," which is released to critical acclaim.

The film concludes with the group's eventual disbandment due to creative differences and personal tensions. Ice Cube goes on to pursue a successful solo career, while Dr. Dre becomes one of the most influential producers in hip-hop history. The movie ends with a sense of closure, but also acknowledges the lasting impact that N.W.A had on the music industry and popular culture.

Throughout the film, the cast delivers strong performances, capturing the complexity and nuance of the real-life characters. The film's soundtrack features many of N.W.A's classic hits, including "Straight Outta Compton," "Fk tha Police," and "Express Yourself." Overall, Straight Outta Compton is a powerful and poignant tribute to one of hip-hop's most influential groups, and a testament to the enduring power of music to inspire and transform.
