title: Descendants
tagline: They're not bad. They're just born that way.
overview: A present-day idyllic kingdom where the benevolent teenage son of King Adam and Queen Belle offers a chance of redemption for the troublemaking offspring of Disney's classic villains: Cruella De Vil (Carlos), Maleficent (Mal), the Evil Queen (Evie) and Jafar (Jay).
plot:
Descendants is a 2015 American musical fantasy made for television, directed and choreographed by Kenny Ortega and written by Josann McGibbon and Sara Parriott. Dove Cameron, Sofia Carson, Booboo Stewart and Cameron Boyce play the teenage children of Maleficent, the Evil Queen, Jafar and Cruella de Vil, with Mitchell Hope, Melanie Paxson, Brenna D'Amico, Sarah Jeffery, Kathy Najimy and Kristin Chenoweth among the supporting cast.

Belle and the Beast now rule the United States of Auradon, a prosperous nation forged from the old kingdoms, while all the villains and their offspring are confined to the Isle of the Lost, a slum island surrounded by a barrier that blocks magic. Their son Ben, soon to be crowned king, invites four children from the isle to attend Auradon Prep: Mal, daughter of Maleficent; Evie, daughter of the Evil Queen; Jay, son of Jafar; and Carlos, son of Cruella. Maleficent orders them to steal the Fairy Godmother's wand, the school headmistress's magic tool, so she can break the barrier and conquer Auradon.

A museum break-in fails, so the four bide their time until Ben's coronation, when the wand will be used. Jay excels on the school's sports team, Carlos conquers his fear of dogs, and Evie, pretending to be shallow to win over Cinderella's son Chad, is encouraged by Doug, the son of Dopey, to be herself. Mal uses her mother's spell book to give Jane, the Fairy Godmother's daughter, and Lonnie, Mulan's daughter, new looks, and feeds Ben a love-potion cookie so she can stand beside him at the ceremony. Instead she begins to fall for him, torn between his kindness and her mother's demands. At the coronation she gives Ben the antidote, only to learn he had already been freed of the spell and loves her anyway. When Jane grabs the wand to make herself beautiful, she accidentally breaches the barrier. Maleficent appears, freezes the crowd and turns into a dragon, but the four, having chosen good, shrink her into a lizard with a counterspell, and Mal hands back the wand.

Filmed in Vancouver and Victoria, British Columbia, the film premiered on Disney Channel on July 31, 2015, to 6.6 million viewers, ranking as one of the most-watched original movies in cable history. Reviews were positive, and it launched a franchise of sequels, series and specials, beginning with Descendants 2 in 2017.

title: Happy New Year
overview: Six would-be thieves enter a prestigious dance competition as a cover for their larger goal of pulling off a major heist.
plot:
Happy New Year is a 2014 Indian Hindi-language heist action comedy written and directed by Farah Khan and produced by Gauri Khan for Red Chillies Entertainment. Shah Rukh Khan, Deepika Padukone, Abhishek Bachchan, Sonu Sood, Boman Irani, Vivaan Shah and Jackie Shroff lead the ensemble cast.

Chandramohan "Charlie" Sharma, a street fighter, has spent eight years planning revenge on tycoon Charan Grover (Shroff). Grover framed Charlie's father, Manohar, for stealing diamonds kept in a vault Manohar had designed. Charlie learns that Grover's diamonds will be stored in Shalimar, the world's most secure vault, beneath the Atlantis hotel in Dubai, on the night the hotel hosts the World Dance Championship. He plans to steal them and frame Grover. He recruits Jag (Sood), a hard-of-hearing explosives expert, and Tammy (Irani), a safecracker who suffers seizures. Both were close to Manohar and helped build Shalimar. Jag's nephew Rohan (Shah) joins as the hacker, and Nandu (Bachchan) joins because he looks exactly like Grover's son Vicky and needs money for his mother's surgery. None of them can dance, so they turn to Mohini (Padukone), a bar dancer who dreams of opening a classical dance school and who falls for Charlie. Through rigging and blackmail, the team qualifies to represent India and travels to Dubai, where at first it is mocked.

Charlie wins the other teams' respect after saving a young Korean dancer from a fall. When the delivery of the diamonds is postponed to New Year's Eve, the judges keep India in the competition as a wild card, and the team reaches the final. Charlie confesses the plan to Mohini, revealing that his father killed himself in prison. Mohini helps them pull off the robbery, but she refuses to skip the final, and the men return to perform with her. Grover is exposed as having stolen his own diamonds and is arrested. Charlie hands him the razor blade his father used, and India wins the title. Charlie has hidden the diamonds in the trophy and later proposes to Mohini with one of them when her dance school opens.

First planned in 2005 and revived in 2012, the film reunited Shah Rukh Khan and Farah Khan after Main Hoon Na and Om Shanti Om. Yash Raj Films released it at Diwali 2014 on a budget of about ₹140 crore. It grossed around ₹394 crore worldwide, making it one of the highest-grossing Indian films at the time, though reviews were mixed: critics liked the cast and humor but not the unoriginal plot.

title: Playing It Cool
tagline: Love... it's a balancing act
overview: A young man meets and instantly falls in love with an engaged woman.
plot:
Playing It Cool is a 2014 American romantic comedy film directed by Michael Showalter and written by Paul Wernick and Rhett Reese. The movie stars Jason Sudeikis, Anna Faris, and Chris Pratt.

The story revolves around Jake (played by Jason Sudeikis), a charming but slightly arrogant baseball player who is dating a beautiful woman named Molly (played by Anna Faris). However, Jake's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets a free-spirited woman named Charlotte (played by Michelle Monaghan) on a plane.

Despite their instant attraction, Jake and Charlotte engage in a game of cat-and-mouse, with each trying to outdo the other in a series of escalating pranks and one-upmanship. As they spend more time together, Jake finds himself falling for Charlotte's charms, but he struggles to balance his feelings with his commitment to Molly.

Meanwhile, Molly is dealing with her own issues - she's struggling to come to terms with the fact that Jake has been lying about his relationship status, and she's starting to realize that she may have fallen in love with him. As the story unfolds, Jake must confront his own emotions and make a choice between his feelings for Charlotte and his commitment to Molly.

Throughout the movie, the characters engage in witty banter and clever pranks, adding to the comedic tone of the film. However, as the plot thickens, the stakes become higher, and the characters are forced to confront their true feelings.

In the end, Jake must make a difficult decision - will he choose the comfort and security of his relationship with Molly, or will he take a chance on love with Charlotte? The movie culminates in a heartwarming and humorous conclusion that leaves the audience rooting for the lovable but flawed protagonist.

Overall, Playing It Cool is a charming and witty romantic comedy that explores themes of love, relationships, and self-discovery. With its talented cast and clever script, the movie is sure to delight audiences looking for a lighthearted and entertaining film experience.

title: Final Girl
tagline: She didn't start it, but she'll finish it.
overview: Veronica, the new girl in town, is lured into the woods by a group of senior boys looking to make her a victim. But the boys don't know that Veronica's been trained to handle herself in surprisingly lethal ways.
plot:
Final Girl is a 2015 American action horror thriller and the directorial debut of the photographer Tyler Shields, written by Adam Prince from a story by Stephen Scarlata, Alejandro Seri and Johnny Silver. Abigail Breslin stars as Veronica, a young woman trained from childhood as an assassin, with Wes Bentley as her mentor William and Alexander Ludwig, Logan Huffman, Cameron Bright and Reece Thompson as a group of murderous high-school boys. Cinedigm released the film in limited cinemas and on video on demand on 14 August 2015.

After the death of her parents, five-year-old Veronica is approached by a mysterious man named William, who offers to take her in and train her for a job meant only for "special" people. He explains that his own wife and child were killed by a very bad man. Veronica accepts, and for the next twelve years she undergoes rigorous training in combat and survival. As her training nears completion, William injects her with a mixture of truth serum and a hallucinogen so that she can confront her greatest fear and understand what her targets will experience. Veronica, who believes herself fearless, discovers that what she fears most is failing her mission.

Meanwhile, four seventeen-year-old boys, Jameson, Daniel, Nelson and Shane, regularly meet at a diner, where their charismatic leader, Jameson, chooses young women for the group to hunt and kill in the woods. Their latest victim is a girl named Gwen. On a reconnaissance mission at the diner, Veronica befriends Shane's girlfriend, Jennifer, confiding her own romantic feelings for the emotionally unavailable William and learning that the boys' friendship is beginning to fracture. Using herself as bait, Veronica accepts a date with Jameson. The boys drive her into the forest, where they play a game of truth or dare and prepare to begin the hunt. But the hunters quickly become the hunted, as Veronica turns their ritual against them, using her training and a hallucinogenic drug to pick them off one by one in the dark woods.

Final Girl received generally negative reviews, with critics praising its stylish visuals and Breslin's performance but finding the story thin and the characters underdeveloped. Many noted that the film, whose title plays on the slasher genre's trope of the lone surviving heroine, was more interested in mood and imagery than in suspense.

title: Unfriended
tagline: Online, your memories last forever. But so do your mistakes.
overview: While video chatting one night, six high school friends receive a Skype message from a classmate who killed herself exactly one year ago. At first they think it's a prank, but when the girl starts revealing the friends' darkest secrets, they realize they are dealing with something out of this world, something that wants them dead.
plot:
Unfriended, originally titled Cybernatural, is a 2014 American supernatural horror film directed by Levan Gabriadze and produced by Timur Bekmambetov. It is one of the best-known examples of the screenlife format: the entire story is presented on the computer screen of its protagonist, through video calls, web browsers, instant messages and social media pages. Shelley Hennig, Moses Storm, Renee Olstead, Will Peltz, Jacob Wysocki and Courtney Halverson play six high school friends, while Heather Sossaman appears as Laura Barns, a classmate whose death haunts the group. The film premiered at the Fantasia International Film Festival in 2014 and was released by Universal Pictures in April 2015.

The story begins in Fresno, California, where teenager Laura Barns took her own life after an anonymous user posted an embarrassing video of her passed out at a party, a clip that went viral and made her the target of relentless online abuse. Exactly one year later, Laura's former best friend Blaire is chatting on Skype with her boyfriend Mitch when they are joined by their friends Jess, Ken and Adam. An unknown account with no profile picture appears in the conversation and cannot be removed, no matter what the group tries.

Blaire discovers that the intruder is using Laura's old account, and the mysterious user begins sending messages from Laura's Facebook profile. Assuming it is a prank, the friends suspect a classmate, Val, and pull her into the chat, but the presence starts exposing their secrets, posting compromising photos and forcing them into a deadly game of "Never Have I Ever", in which each confession reveals betrayals, lies and their roles in the cruelty that drove Laura to her death. Anyone who tries to log off or disobeys the entity dies in a gruesome way, and as the friendships disintegrate, the survivors are forced to confront who was really responsible for the video that destroyed Laura.

The film uses its unusual format to address cyberbullying, online shaming and the permanence of digital actions, drawing tension from loading screens, frozen video feeds and messages typed and deleted in real time.

Made on a budget of about one million dollars, Unfriended was a major box-office success, grossing more than sixty million dollars worldwide. Critics were divided but often praised its inventive approach, and it was followed by the stand-alone sequel Unfriended: Dark Web in 2018.

title: Moana
tagline: The ocean is calling.
overview: In Ancient Polynesia, when a terrible curse incurred by Maui reaches an impetuous Chieftain's daughter's island, she answers the Ocean's call to seek out the demigod to set things right.
plot:
Moana (2016) is an animated adventure film that explores several themes that are both universally relatable and culturally specific to Polynesian communities.

One of the primary themes of Moana is the concept of identity and self-discovery. The protagonist, Moana, is a young girl who feels an insatiable call to explore the ocean and discover her true purpose in life. As she sets sail on her journey, she must navigate her own identity and confront the expectations placed upon her by her community.

Another significant theme in Moana is the importance of family and tradition. Moana's island, Motunui, is a tight-knit community that values its ancestral heritage and cultural traditions. However, as Moana embarks on her journey, she must also learn to balance her own desires with the needs of her family and community.

The film also explores the theme of perseverance and determination in the face of adversity. Moana faces numerous challenges, including treacherous seas, fierce monsters, and her own self-doubt. However, through her bravery and resilience, she is able to overcome these obstacles and achieve her goals.

Furthermore, Moana touches on the theme of colonialism and cultural appropriation. The film's depiction of European explorers and their impact on Polynesian cultures is a commentary on the historical exploitation and erasure of indigenous cultures. However, it also highlights the importance of preserving and celebrating one's own cultural heritage.

Finally, Moana features a strong female protagonist who embodies qualities such as courage, compassion, and wisdom. The film celebrates women's empowerment and encourages young girls to be confident in their abilities and pursue their passions.

Overall, Moana is a beautifully crafted film that explores complex themes and emotions through its engaging storyline and memorable characters.

title: Ice Age: Collision Course
tagline: One small step. One giant mess.
overview: Set after the events of Continental Drift, Scrat's epic pursuit of his elusive acorn catapults him outside of Earth, where he accidentally sets off a series of cosmic events that transform and threaten the planet. To save themselves from peril, Manny, Sid, Diego, and the rest of the herd leave their home and embark on a quest full of thrills and spills, highs and lows, laughter and adventure while traveling to exotic new lands and locations.
plot:
Ice Age: Collision Course is a 2016 American animated adventure comedy film directed by Michael Thurmeier and written by Michael Wilson, Michael Berg and Yoni Brenner. Produced by 20th Century Fox Animation and Blue Sky Studios, it is the fifth installment in the Ice Age series, following Ice Age: Continental Drift (2012). Ray Romano, John Leguizamo, Denis Leary, Josh Peck, Simon Pegg, Seann William Scott, Jennifer Lopez and Queen Latifah reprise their voice roles, joined by Jessie J and Adam DeVine.

Peaches, the daughter of the mammoths Manny and Ellie, is engaged to Julian, a cheerful mammoth whom Manny finds annoying and considers incapable of protecting her, and Manny is even more upset to learn that the couple want to travel the world after the wedding. Diego and Shira are hoping to start a family, and Sid is dumped by his girlfriend just as he is about to propose. Meanwhile Scrat's never-ending pursuit of his acorn has propelled him into outer space aboard an abandoned spaceship, where his antics send a giant asteroid hurtling toward Earth. As meteors begin to rain down on Manny and Ellie's anniversary, the herd takes shelter in a cave and is reunited with the adventurous weasel Buck, who has found an ancient stone pillar in the underground dinosaur world. According to its carvings, asteroids have caused two mass extinctions in the past, always striking the same spot, and Buck believes a solution may be found there. Pursued by a trio of flying dromaeosaurs who hope to survive the catastrophe and inherit the planet, the herd sets off for the impact site. On the way, Buck discovers that the asteroids are magnetic and devises a plan to launch a mass of smaller fragments into orbit to pull the big one off course. The journey leads them to Geotopia, a community of long-lived animals living inside a fallen asteroid, where Sid finds a new admirer in a sloth named Brooke, but the community's leader, Shangri Llama, refuses to surrender the crystals that keep his people young, and the herd must find a way to save the world while Manny learns to accept Julian.

The film received generally negative reviews; on Rotten Tomatoes, only 18% of 120 critics' reviews are positive, ranking it as the lowest-rated Ice Age film, with a consensus calling it unoriginal and unfunny. It still grossed $408 million worldwide against a $105 million production budget.

title: Avatar Spirits
tagline: In 2002, two friends set out to create a groundbreaking animated epic. This is their story.
overview: Bryan Konietzko and Michael Dante DiMartino, co-creators of the hit television series, Avatar: The Last Airbender, reflect on the creation of the masterful series.
plot:
Avatar Spirits is a 2010 American documentary film directed by Kurt Mattila about the making of the Nickelodeon animated series Avatar: The Last Airbender. Produced by Nickelodeon Productions with Prologue Pictures and running about half an hour, it was released in June 2010 and features the series' co-creators, Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko, reflecting on how their show came together, alongside interviews with many of the artists, musicians and consultants who worked on it. Its tagline sums up its approach: in 2002, two friends set out to create a groundbreaking animated epic, and this is their story.

The series it chronicles aired on Nickelodeon for three seasons from 2005 to 2008 and follows Aang, a twelve-year-old boy who is the last of the Air Nomads and the Avatar, the only person able to bend all four elements. The documentary traces this world back to a single sketch by Konietzko showing a bald boy, a tall animal with an arrow on its head and a robot monkey with a futuristic staff. The arrow migrated to the boy's head, and the creatures evolved into the characters Appa and Momo. At about the same time, DiMartino had become fascinated by Ernest Shackleton's struggle to survive in the Antarctic, and combining that polar setting with the idea of "fire people" attacking "water people" led to the concept of four nations.

The film describes the pitch to Nickelodeon development executive Eric Coleman, the demanding production of the pilot, for which Konietzko spent several months in South Korea and designs had to be simplified, and the order of thirteen episodes that followed its success with young test audiences. It then turns to the wider crew. Martial arts instructors Sifu Kisu and Manuel Rodríguez explain how real fighting styles, filmed in sparring sessions, provided the basis for the animated bending; director Giancarlo Volpe recalls the cinematic camera angles the creators demanded; Jeremy Zuckerman and Benjamin Wynn of the Track Team describe the unusual instruments behind the show's music and sound; and voice director Andrea Romano explains how she guided the actors' performances.

The documentary closes with the making of the finale, which the creators always intended as the definitive end of the story. To make it their best work, the Track Team recorded a live string orchestra for the first time, and the crew, with friends and family, gathered at the Paramount theater to watch the ending on a big screen.

overview: Arthur Bishop thought he had put his murderous past behind him when his most formidable foe kidnaps the love of his life. Now he is forced to travel the globe to complete three impossible assassinations, and do what he does best, make them look like accidents.
plot:
Mechanic: Resurrection is a 2016 action thriller film directed by Dennis Gansel and starring Jason Statham as the titular character, Arthur Bishop. The movie follows Bishop's latest mission to rescue his mentor, Max (Tony Jaa), who has been kidnapped by a powerful crime lord named Gabriel (Michael Angarano).

The story begins with Bishop, a skilled assassin and mechanic, living in Bangkok, Thailand. He is approached by a wealthy businessman named Henry (Hugo Weaving) who asks for his help in rescuing Max, a former ally who has gone missing. Bishop agrees to take on the mission, but soon discovers that Gabriel, a ruthless crime lord, is behind Max's kidnapping.

As Bishop delves deeper into the world of high-stakes crime, he meets a young woman named Sarah (Hannah Hughes), Henry's daughter, who becomes his unlikely ally. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to rescue Max and take down Gabriel's operation.

Throughout the movie, Bishop faces off against Gabriel's henchmen in intense hand-to-hand combat sequences, showcasing his exceptional fighting skills. Along the way, he also encounters other characters, including a mysterious woman named Anna (Mia Goth), who seems to be hiding secrets of her own.

As the story unfolds, Bishop and Sarah navigate through the dark underbelly of Bangkok's crime scene, uncovering a complex web of corruption and deceit. They eventually track down Gabriel's operation to an abandoned warehouse on the outskirts of the city, where they engage in a fierce battle with Gabriel's men.

In the climactic final showdown, Bishop faces off against Gabriel, who reveals himself to be a former ally turned enemy. The two engage in a intense fight, with Bishop using his mechanical skills to outmaneuver and overpower Gabriel. In the end, Bishop emerges victorious, rescuing Max and bringing Gabriel's operation down.

Throughout the movie, Statham delivers his signature blend of action and humor, making Mechanic: Resurrection a thrilling ride for fans of the genre. The film's visuals are stunning, with breathtaking action sequences and impressive stunts that showcase Bishop's skills as a mechanic and assassin.

Overall, Mechanic: Resurrection is an adrenaline-fueled thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and suspenseful storytelling. With Statham at the helm, the movie is a must-see for fans of the Mechanic franchise and action enthusiasts alike.

title: The Jungle Book
tagline: The legend will never be the same.
overview: A man-cub named Mowgli fostered by wolves. After a threat from the tiger Shere Khan, Mowgli is forced to flee the jungle, by which he embarks on a journey of self discovery with the help of the panther, Bagheera and the free-spirited bear, Baloo.
plot:
The Jungle Book is a 2016 American live-action adaptation of Rudyard Kipling's 1894 collection of stories, The Jungle Book. Directed by Jon Favreau and produced by Walt Disney Pictures, the film stars Neel Sethi as Mowgli, a young boy raised by wolves in the jungle.

The story begins with a human infant, Mowgli, found by a pack of wolves led by Akela (Idris Elba) and Raksha (Lupita Nyong'o), who adopt him as one of their own. The wolf pack teaches Mowgli how to survive in the jungle, but he is also aware of his human identity.

As Mowgli grows up, he faces various challenges, including encounters with Shere Khan (Ben Kingsley), a Bengal tiger with a vendetta against humans. Shere Khan had been wounded by a human boy as a cub and seeks revenge on all humans. The wolf pack warns Mowgli about the dangers of Shere Khan, but he is also curious about his human past.

Mowgli's life in the jungle is disrupted when Baloo (Bill Murray), a laid-back sloth bear, and Bagheera (Neel Sethi's voice double, Idris Elba's voice) arrive. They inform Mowgli that it's time for him to leave the jungle and return to his human village.

However, Shere Khan discovers Mowgli's true identity and plots to kill him. The wolf pack and Baloo help Mowgli evade Shere Khan's attacks, but they are eventually forced to flee into the jungle.

As Mowgli navigates the dangers of the jungle, he learns valuable lessons about loyalty, friendship, and his own identity. He also discovers that he has a special connection with humans, which sets him apart from the other wolves.

In the end, Mowgli must confront Shere Khan in a final showdown. With the help of Baloo and Bagheera, Mowgli outsmarts Shere Khan and returns to his human village, where he is welcomed back by his family.

The film features stunning visual effects, showcasing the beauty and danger of the jungle. The cast delivers strong performances, bringing depth and nuance to their characters. The Jungle Book (2016) is a thrilling adventure that explores themes of identity, belonging, and the power of friendship.

Overall, the 2016 adaptation of The Jungle Book is a captivating retelling of Kipling's classic tale, with impressive visuals, memorable performances, and a story that will keep audiences on the edge of their seats.

title: Whiskey Tango Foxtrot
tagline: From the headlines to the front lines.
overview: In 2002, cable news producer Kim Barker decides to shake up her routine by taking a daring new assignment in Kabul, Afghanistan. Dislodged from her comfortable American lifestyle, Barker finds herself in the middle of an out-of-control war zone. plot:
In 2003 New York City, Kim Baker is a struggling television journalist covering low-profile stories. To help her career, she takes a short assignment as a war correspondent in Afghanistan during Operation Enduring Freedom, to the disappointment of her boyfriend Chris.
Assigned to modest living quarters with other international journalists, Kim befriends noted BBC correspondent Tanya Vanderpoel and lecherous Scottish freelance photographer Iain MacKelpie. She adjusts to her new duties aided by her Afghan "fixer" Fahim Ahmadzai. She elicits frank remarks on camera from soldiers questioning the value of their assignment and puts herself in harm's way to capture combat incidents on video. Marine General Hollanek sees her as an inexperienced nuisance. Despite the danger, Kim stays in Afghanistan for years beyond her original assignment. She catches Chris with another woman during a middle-of-the-night video call, ending their relationship and her sexual flirtation with Iain develops into something more meaningful.
Although Afghan Islamic society places restrictive roles on women, she uses her sex to her advantage and gains access to female villagers who have been sabotaging the US-built well because they welcome the daily walk to the river away from the men. She uses her own sexuality to develop Afghan Attorney General Ali Massoud Sadiq as a news source. Fahim, who treated opium addicts before the war, cautions her that danger can be as dangerous as a drug. Despite their mutual friendliness, Kim competes with other journalists for stories and resources from their employers. title: Mr. Holmes
tagline: The man behind the myth.
overview: In 1947, long-retired and near the end of his life, Sherlock Holmes grapples with an unreliable memory and must rely on his housekeeper's son as he revisits the still-unsolved case that led to his retirement.
plot:
Mr. Holmes is a 2015 mystery drama directed by Bill Condon, based on Mitch Cullin's 2005 novel A Slight Trick of the Mind. Ian McKellen stars as an elderly Sherlock Holmes, with Laura Linney as his housekeeper Mrs Munro, Milo Parker as her son Roger, Hiroyuki Sanada as Tamiki Umezaki and Hattie Morahan as Ann Kelmot. The film premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival in February 2015 and was released in British cinemas in June and in the United States in July 2015.

In 1947, the ninety-three-year-old Holmes lives in retirement on a farm in Sussex, where he keeps bees, looked after by the widowed Mrs Munro and her bright young son Roger. He has just returned from a trip to Japan, where he obtained prickly ash, a plant he hopes will slow the decline of his memory. Dissatisfied with Dr. Watson's fictionalised account of his final case, he wants to write the true story, but he can no longer remember how it ended. As Holmes teaches Roger to care for the bees, he grows fond of the boy's curiosity and intelligence, and Roger's questions help him piece together his memories.

In flashbacks set some thirty years earlier, after Watson has married and left Baker Street, a man named Thomas Kelmot asks Holmes to find out why his wife Ann has grown distant after two miscarriages. Following her through London, Holmes observes behaviour that appears to suggest she is planning to kill her husband, but he deduces that she is in fact planning her own death. When he confronts her, she asks whether they might share their loneliness together, but Holmes sends her back to her husband. Her subsequent suicide leaves him consumed by guilt, and he retires from detective work. A second thread recalls his visit to Japan, where Umezaki reveals that he brought Holmes there to learn why his father abandoned his family. In the present, a crisis involving Roger and the bees forces Holmes to recognise the value of human connection over pure logic.

The film portrays Holmes as a vulnerable old man confronting memory loss, regret and loneliness, rather than as an infallible detective, and McKellen's performance drew particular praise.

Mr. Holmes received positive reviews, with about 88 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it grossed about 29 million dollars worldwide.

The group faces numerous challenges, including harsh weather conditions, hostile Native American tribes, and treacherous terrain.

Glass's quest for revenge against those who betrayed and left him for dead becomes the central focus of the film. He sets out on a perilous journey across the wilderness, facing numerous obstacles, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and hostile Native American tribes.

As Glass navigates the unforgiving environment, he encounters John Fitzgerald (Tom Hardy), a fellow trapper who had been part of the expedition but was also left for dead. However, instead of helping Glass, Fitzgerald betrays him and steals his valuable possessions, including his rifle and supplies.

Glass's determination to survive and exact revenge on those who wronged him drives him forward, despite the numerous challenges he faces. He encounters various characters, including a Native American tribe that takes him in and teaches him their ways, as well as a group of fur traders who are also seeking to exploit the region's resources.

Throughout his journey, Glass undergoes a transformation from a broken and defeated man to a strong and determined individual. His physical and emotional scars serve as a reminder of his past traumas, but they also fuel his determination to survive and exact revenge on those who wronged him.

The film's climax features an intense and brutal confrontation between Glass and Fitzgerald, which ultimately leads to the death of both men. In the end, Glass emerges victorious, having survived against all odds and exacted his revenge on those who betrayed him.

The Revenant is a visually stunning film that showcases the harsh beauty of the American wilderness. The cinematography is breathtaking, with sweeping vistas and intimate close-ups that immerse the viewer in the world of the film. The performances by DiCaprio and Hardy are also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, The Revenant is a powerful and haunting film that explores themes of survival, revenge, and redemption in the face of unimaginable hardship.

As Nick and Jenny delve deeper into the mystery of the tomb, they realize that Ahmanet is not just a simple mummy, but a powerful and malevolent entity who can control the minds of others. plot:
Parasyte: Part 1 is a Japanese science fiction action film of 2014 directed by Takashi Yamazaki, the first of two films adapted from Hitoshi Iwaaki's manga series Parasyte and followed by Parasyte: Part 2. Shota Sometani stars as the high school student Shinichi Izumi, with Sadao Abe as the voice of Migi, the creature living in his hand, Eri Fukatsu as the teacher Ryoko Tamiya, Ai Hashimoto as Shinichi's girlfriend Satomi Murano and Kimiko Yo as Shinichi's mother Nobuko.

Mysterious alien organisms known as parasites begin invading Earth, burrowing into human beings and taking over their brains. One tries to enter the head of Shinichi, but because he is wearing headphones it fails and instead takes over his right hand. As a result Shinichi keeps his own mind, unlike the other victims. He befriends the creature and names it Migi, Japanese for "right". The parasites secretly feed on humans, and many of them are repelled by Shinichi's two minds sharing one body and try to kill him. One parasite has taken over his teacher, Ryoko Tamiya, who is far more rational than the others and curious about human life; to study it, she has become pregnant by a fellow parasite, Mr. A, and explains that her baby will be an ordinary human.

When Mr. A's attack on Shinichi fails and his host body is destroyed, he moves into Shinichi's mother, Nobuko. She returns home and gravely wounds her son, but Migi saves him by repairing his heart with its own cells, spreading its particles throughout his body. From then on, Shinichi's personality begins to blend with Migi's cool detachment, and he drifts away from Satomi. Meanwhile Tamiya's ally Hirokawa runs for mayor to turn the city into a haven for parasites. Another parasite, Shimada, transfers to Shinichi's school and seems friendly, but when a student uncovers his secret he slaughters the pupils. After Satomi wounds and disfigures him, leaving him unable to control himself, Tamiya abandons him and Shinichi kills him. Tamiya then tells Shinichi where to find the creature in his mother's body. When they meet, Nobuko manages to overcome the parasite long enough for her son to kill her. In an epilogue, Hirokawa wins the mayoral election, the formidable parasite Goto appears, and Shinichi visits Satomi in hospital while an unknown figure secretly records him talking to Migi.

Closing the Tokyo International Film Festival before its release in November 2014, the film topped the Japanese box office in its opening weekend.

As the authorities prepare a large-scale operation to exterminate the parasites in city hall, Shinichi faces Gotō, a powerful parasite made up of several organisms within one body. The final battle forces Shinichi to rely on his bond with Migi and his own humanity, while Tamiya's choices shed new light on what separates humans from the creatures that hunt them.

The film was a box-office success in Japan, although reviews were mixed. title: My Old Lady
tagline: He's in the will. She's in the way.
overview: Mathias Gold is a down-on-his-luck New Yorker who inherits a Parisian apartment from his estranged father. But when he arrives in France to sell the vast domicile, he's shocked to discover a live-in tenant who is not prepared to budge. His apartment is a viager—an ancient French real estate system with complex rules pertaining to its resale—and the feisty Englishwoman Mathilde Girard, who has lived in the apartment with her daughter Chloé for many years, can by contract collect monthly payments from Mathias until her death.
plot:
Mathias Gold, a down-and-out New Yorker, inherits a large, valuable apartment in Paris from his estranged father. He spends all the money he has on an airplane ticket to Paris, planning to sell the apartment. Once there, however, he discovers that an elderly woman, Mathilde Girard, lives in the apartment and that his father purchased it from her 43 years ago under a contract known in French property law as a "viager": the buyer pays a reduced price for the apartment, but the seller may continue living in it for the remainder of their life, during which time the buyer must pay the seller a fixed monthly amount. Mathias, as the owner, will thus be required to pay Mathilde €2,400 a month until she dies, unless he sells the contract to someone else.
Mathias has no money, but Mathilde allows him to stay in the apartment in exchange for his father's gold watch. That night, Mathias encounters Mathilde's daughter, Chloé, and learns she is living there, too; she is initially hostile toward him. Chloé invites Mathias to a café, and he invites developer François Roy, who has already discussed buying the apartment with him, to join them. Roy, whom Chloé already knows and despises, offers to buy Mathias's contract from him; Mathias asks for a week to consider the offer. Chloé tells Mathias that if he accepts the offer, she will be thrown out on the street when her mother dies. Mathias eventually accepts Roy's offer pending signature of the contract.
Mathias learns Mathilde and his father had a long-lasting affair that began when they were young; she was married to a wealthy businessman, while Mathias's father was penniless and had only just met his mother. Mathilde stayed with her husband for Chloé's sake. Mathias tells Mathilde how her affair with his father affected him: he felt unloved and ignored, so he turned to drink and had a string of failed marriages, even trying to commit suicide at age 40. Mathilde says she never saw his father again after Mathias's mother died.
Chloé is having an affair with a married man, which Mathias discovers and even tries to use to blackmail her into waiving his monthly payments. Reflecting upon how her mother's affair affected her and Mathias, Chloé breaks off her own. She tells Mathias she was 10 when she became aware of what was going on, but could do nothing about it. Mathias replies that at that same age, he had to act to prevent his mother from committing suicide. She tries to console him, but he pushes her away.
Mathilde seeks to assuage her guilt by claiming that Mathias's mother must have known and even approved of her affair with his father. When he informs Mathilde that his mother attempted suicide several times before finally succeeding when he was 19, she collapses from shock, having been told his mother died from an illness.
Mathias and Chloé share a kiss and spend the night together.

title: The Admiral: Roaring Currents
tagline: 12 ships against a fleet of 330.
overview: The film mainly follows the famous 1597 Battle of Myeongryang during the Japanese invasion of Korea 1592-1598, where the iconic Joseon admiral Yi Sun-sin managed to destroy a total of 133 Japanese warships with only 13 ships remaining in his command. The battle, which took place in the Myeongryang Strait off the southwest coast of the Korean Peninsula, is considered one of the greatest victories of Yi.
plot:
The film revolves around the titular Battle of Myeongryang around 1597, which is regarded as one of legendary Joseon Admiral Yi Sun-sin's most remarkable naval victories. He led only 12 ships under his command to a heroic victory against an invading Japanese fleet of 133 vessels.
At the onset of the battle at their base in Haenam, the Japanese invaders under Tōdō Takatora are confident that their planned expedition to Hansong to capture King Seonjo will be rather straightforward. However, they remain reserved over the news that Joseon's greatest admiral, Yi Sun-sin, has been restored to his former command after the disaster at Chilcheollyang, which has reduced the Korean navy to a mere dozen battle-ready ships. To ensure the success of the operation, Hideyoshi sends one of his finest naval war leaders to Joseon, Kurushima Michifusa, the commander of the Murakami Clan Navy who is an expert in naval combat but enjoys a shaky reputation among his fellow daimyō as a pirate. One of the admirals of the Japanese Left Army, Wakizaka, first meets Kurushima and his lieutenant, Kimura, while he finishes off the remnants of a group of Joseon soldiers. He especially distrusts Kurushima and draws his sword on him several times, especially after the latter insults him by shaming his defeat at Hansan Island. Later, Kurushima and Haru, his sharpshooter, drink sake as Kurushima elaborates on his personal vendetta against Yi Sun-sin, stating that his brother Michiyuki had been killed by the latter earlier in the war.
In the meantime, Yi Sun-sin is facing the despair mounting among his officers and troops. Facing an enemy force that far outnumbers them and seeing no reasonable chance of success in the inevitable clash even with one single turtle ship remaining, many consider the fight lost before it has even started. Despite his outwardly indifferent demeanor, Yi is hard-pressed to maintain morale among his men and desperate to find a solution to his problem. However, the breaking point seems to be reached when General Bae Seol, the deserter of Chilcheollyang, burns the turtle ship and has his men try to assassinate Yi. Although Yi escapes and Bae is killed for his act of treachery, the ship is lost, which boosts confidence among the Japanese and further dispirits Yi's troops. To seek an answer, Yi travels to the Myeongryang Strait, an area notorious for its strong and treacherous currents, which the Japanese intend to cross on their way to Hansong. Later, he confides in his son Hoe that to win the fight, he must turn the fear paralyzing his men into courage.
Upon hearing that the departure of the Japanese attack fleet is imminent, Yi abandons his base and moves to Usuyeong after burning the naval facilities to the ground. The next morning, Yi's fleet arrives in the strait and is shortly met by the Japanese, who are using the morning tide to move into the channel, with Kurushima leading the vanguard.

overview: A teenager finds himself transported to an island where he must help protect a group of orphans with special powers from creatures intent on destroying them.
plot:
Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children is a 2016 American fantasy adventure film directed by Tim Burton, based on the 2011 novel of the same name by Ransom Riggs. The movie stars Asa Butterfield, Eva Green, and Terence Stamp.

The story begins with Jake Portman (Asa Butterfield), an orphan who lives with his cruel and neglectful foster parents, Mr. and Mrs. Bugg. On his 16th birthday, Jake receives a letter from a lawyer's office informing him that he is the sole beneficiary of a mysterious inheritance: a large sum of money and a peculiar mansion in Wales.

Jake travels to Wales, where he discovers the mansion, which turns out to be the home of Miss Peregrine (Eva Green), a mysterious and enigmatic caretaker. She reveals to Jake that his grandfather, Abraham Portman, was a famous photographer who discovered a magical island called Cairnholm Island, where children with extraordinary abilities, known as "peculiarities," live.

Miss Peregrine explains that these children are being hunted by monstrous creatures known as the Hollows, which feed on human flesh. The peculiarity Jake possesses is his ability to see and communicate with the dead. He also discovers that he has a special connection to his grandfather's past and the mysterious island.

As Jake spends more time at the mansion, he learns about the history of the peculiaries and their struggles against the Hollows. He also meets other peculiar children, including Emma Bloom (Maddie Harris), a fire-starting girl; Olive Llewellyn (Lora Akinley), a shape-shifting boy; and Horace Burroughs (Samson Kayo), a boy with superhuman strength.

However, their peaceful existence is disrupted when Jake discovers that the Hollows are closing in on the island. He also learns that his grandfather's death was not an accident but a deliberate act to protect him from the Hollows.

As the story unfolds, Jake and Miss Peregrine embark on a perilous journey to Cairnholm Island, where they must confront the monstrous creatures and uncover the secrets of the peculiaries' past. Along the way, Jake discovers more about his grandfather's life and the mysterious island, which holds many secrets and surprises.

The movie culminates in an action-packed sequence as Jake and Miss Peregrine face off against the Hollows on the island. In a thrilling finale, Jake uses his newfound understanding of the peculiaries' abilities to defeat the monsters and save the children.

In the end, Jake returns home with a newfound appreciation for his grandfather's legacy and the peculiar children who have become like family to him. The movie concludes with Jake reflecting on the lessons he has learned about acceptance, love, and the power of being different.

Overall, Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children is a visually stunning and imaginative film that explores themes of identity, community, and self-acceptance. With its unique blend of fantasy and adventure, it has become a beloved classic among fans of Tim Burton's films.

title: Fallen
tagline: Some angels are destined to fall.
overview: Lucinda Price is sent to a reform academy under the assumption that she has killed a boy. There, she meets two mysterious boys, Cam and Daniel, to whom she feels drawn to both. But as the love triangle unfurls, it is Daniel that Luce cannot keep herself away from, and things begin to take a darker turn when she finds out his true identity.
plot:
Fallen is a 2016 romantic fantasy drama directed by Scott Hicks and based on Lauren Kate's 2009 young adult novel of the same name, the first book in her Fallen series. Addison Timlin stars as Lucinda "Luce" Price, with Jeremy Irvine as Daniel Grigori, Harrison Gilbertson as Cam, Lola Kirke, Juliet Aubrey and Joely Richardson. The film opened in several countries, including Malaysia, the Philippines and Singapore, in November 2016, but its American release was delayed until September 2017, when Relativity Media distributed it.

Luce is sent to Sword and Cross, a gloomy reform school for troubled teenagers, after she is blamed for the death of a boy named Trevor, who died in a fire after she kissed him. She remembers seeing strange shadows around them before the fire and fears that she is cursed. At her new school she meets an assortment of students: the charming Cam, who quickly shows an interest in her; the eccentric Arriane, who takes her under her wing; the hostile Molly; the friendly Penn; and the brooding Daniel Grigori, to whom she feels an immediate and inexplicable attraction despite his efforts to push her away. She also meets Miss Sophia, a teacher of religious studies.

The school psychiatrist tells Luce that she can leave if she agrees to take antipsychotic medication, but strange events keep happening around her, including a near-fatal accident with a falling statue of an angel. Torn between Cam's open flirtation and her mysterious connection to Daniel, Luce begins to research his past with Penn's help and discovers evidence suggesting that she and Daniel have met many times before, in different eras. She eventually learns that Daniel and several of her schoolmates are fallen angels and that she has been reincarnated repeatedly, each time falling in love with Daniel and dying before their love can be fulfilled. As a battle between heaven and hell draws closer to Sword and Cross, Luce must discover who she really is and whom she can trust.

The film was a critical and commercial failure. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 7 percent approval rating based on 14 reviews, with an average score of 3.2 out of 10. Several critics compared it unfavorably with earlier supernatural teen romances, and its long-delayed American release did little to attract an audience.

plot:
Sinister 2 is a 2015 American supernatural horror film directed by Scott Derrickson and written by C. Robert Cargill and Derrickson. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2012 film Sinister, which was also produced by Gramercy Pictures.

The story follows Ellison Oswalt (Ethan Hawke), a true-crime writer who has moved his family from Texas to Kansas City, Missouri, in an attempt to escape the traumatic events of the past. However, their new life is disrupted when they discover that their home contains a box of disturbing home movies that seem to be connected to a series of murders.

As Ellison delves deeper into the mystery, he becomes convinced that the killer is still at large and is using the home movies as a way to taunt him. He enlists the help of his wife Tracy (Juliet Rylance) and their daughter Kinsey (Lochlyn Munro), who has been struggling with her own dark past.

The family soon discovers that they are not alone in their new home, as they begin to experience strange occurrences and supernatural events. They also meet a mysterious woman named Bughuul (James Ransone), who seems to be connected to the murders and is using the home movies to lure victims into his trap.

As Ellison delves deeper into the mystery, he becomes increasingly obsessed with uncovering the truth behind the murders and the identity of the killer. However, his obsession puts his family in grave danger, and they must fight for survival against a supernatural force that seems to be beyond their control.

Throughout the movie, Derrickson explores themes of trauma, grief, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human understanding. The film's climax features a tense showdown between Ellison and Bughuul, as the true nature of the killer is revealed and the family must confront the darkness head-on.

Ultimately, Sinister 2 is a chilling horror movie that builds on the success of its predecessor while introducing new themes and characters to the franchise. While it may not be as groundbreaking as the original, it delivers plenty of scares and tension, making it a must-see for fans of the genre.

title: The Light Between Oceans
tagline: Love demands everything
overview: A lighthouse keeper and his wife living off the coast of Western Australia raise a baby they rescue from an adrift rowboat.
plot:
The Light Between Oceans is a 2016 romantic period drama written and directed by Derek Cianfrance, based on the 2012 novel by M. L. Stedman. An international co-production, it stars Michael Fassbender as Tom Sherbourne, Alicia Vikander as Isabel Graysmark and Rachel Weisz as Hannah Roennfeldt, with Bryan Brown and Jack Thompson. It tells the story of a lighthouse keeper and his wife who rescue an infant adrift at sea and raise her as their own.

In 1918, Tom Sherbourne, a withdrawn veteran of the First World War, takes a position as the keeper of the lighthouse on Janus Rock, a remote island off the coast of Australia. He falls in love with Isabel, a spirited young woman from the nearby town, and they marry and settle on the island. Their happiness is shattered when Isabel suffers two miscarriages. Shortly after the second, a rowboat washes ashore carrying a dead man and a crying baby girl. Tom knows that he must report the discovery, but the grieving Isabel persuades him to keep the child and pretend she is their own. Tom buries the man on the island, and the couple name the baby Lucy.

When the couple take Lucy to the mainland to be christened, Tom sees a woman, Hannah Roennfeldt, mourning at a grave dedicated to her husband and infant daughter, who were lost at sea on the very day the boat reached Janus Rock. Realizing that Lucy is almost certainly Hannah's child, Tom is consumed by guilt and secretly sends Hannah a message assuring her that her daughter is safe and loved. As Lucy grows up, the couple's deception becomes harder to sustain, and Tom's conscience sets in motion a chain of events that will test the marriage, the bond between mother and child and the meaning of forgiveness.

Cianfrance shot the film on location in New Zealand and Tasmania, emphasizing the isolation of the lighthouse and the elemental landscapes surrounding it.

The film premiered in competition at the Venice International Film Festival on September 1, 2016, and was released in the United States the next day by Touchstone Pictures. It received mixed reviews, with about 62 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 60, though the lead performances were praised. It grossed about 26 million dollars worldwide against a budget of 20 million.

overview: In the aftermath of the Fourth Impact, stranded without their Evangelions, Shinji, Asuka and Rei find refuge in one of the rare pockets of humanity that still exist on the ruined planet Earth. plot:
Evangelion: 3.0+1.0 Thrice Upon a Time is a 2021 Japanese animated science fiction film directed by Masayuki, and produced by Studio Khara. The movie serves as the final installment of the Rebuild of Evangelion series, which reimagines the original Neon Genesis Evangelion story.

The film takes place four years after the events of Evangelion: 3.0+1.01 Thrice Upon a Time. Shinji Ikari, now 17 years old, is struggling to cope with his emotional trauma and feelings of inadequacy. He is still haunted by the memories of his mother, Yui, and his relationship with Rei Ayanami.

title: Beasts of No Nation
tagline: Child. Captive. Killer.
overview: Based on the experiences of Agu, a child fighting in the civil war of an unnamed, fictional West African country. Follows Agu's journey as he's forced to join a group of soldiers. While he fears his commander and many of the men around him, his fledgling childhood has been brutally shattered by the war raging through his country, and he is at first torn between conflicting revulsion and fascination.
plot:
A young boy, Agu, lives in a small West African village with his parents and siblings, located within a "buffer zone" enforced by ECOMOG troops. The village is informed that the government has fallen and that military-aligned rebels have seized control of the country. With rebel forces headed toward the village, many people flee to the country's capital for safety. Agu's father buys safe transport for his wife and two youngest children, but has to stay behind with Agu and his eldest son. Rebel and government forces fight in and around Agu's village. While the rebel soldiers flee, government forces round up the remaining villagers and execute them, but Agu escapes into the jungle.
After wandering for a while, Agu is caught up in a guerrilla skirmish. The Native Defense Forces (NDF), a rising rebel faction in the country, adopt Agu into their ranks. Agu's battalion is led by the Commandant, who takes Agu under his wing. Following a brutal initiation process in which Agu hacks an innocent captive to death with a machete, Agu becomes a fully fledged member of the militia. Agu befriends another young NDF child soldier, Strika, who never speaks. One night, the Commandant summons Agu to his quarters and rapes him. Strika, another of the Commandant's rape victims, comforts him. Preacher, an older soldier, gives Agu brown-brown to lift his mood. Agu and Strika take part in a number of bloody battles and ambushes. During one of the raids, Agu, under the influence of brown-brown, mistakes a villager for his mother. He exclaims that he has found her and clings to her while the other members of the group declare that they want to rape her. The woman does not recognize Agu, and he calls her a witch woman. Agu then shoots the woman while she is being raped.
The battalion's many victories earn them a summons to the rebel headquarters, where the Commandant, accompanied by Agu, Strika, and a few other soldiers, goes to meet with the NDF leader, Dada Goodblood. Goodblood, who stresses the importance of public image in the wake of the conflict becoming world news, denies the Commandant his promised promotion to General and removes him from command. The Commandant's lieutenant, Two I-C, will take control of the battalion, and the Commandant will be made Deputy Chief of Security under the leader. The Commandant views this as an insult and leaves to "celebrate" with his men at a brothel. While the adult soldiers spend the night with the brothel's women, one of the women shoots Two I-C. Two I-C accuses the Commandant of orchestrating the incident before dying, while the Commandant insists it must have been a botched attempt against himself. The prostitute professes that it was an accident, but the Commandant and his men shoot the women and leave the city.
Now on the run from their own faction as well as their enemies, the battalion suffers heavy losses. Air strikes and supply shortages kill Strika and many others.

title: The Secret Scripture
tagline: Love is not a sin.
overview: The hidden memoir of an elderly woman confined to a mental hospital reveals the history of her passionate yet tortured life, and of the religious and political upheavals in Ireland during the 1920s and 30s.
plot:
The film alternates between the early years of World War II and the end of the 20th century.
Rose McNulty (Vanessa Redgrave) has been a patient in the Sligo Regional Mental Hospital for 50 years since being accused of murdering her baby in 1942. The facility is scheduled for demolition. Dr. Stephen Grene (Eric Bana) is a psychiatrist who, at the request of the local Catholic Church, is evaluating whether Rose should be transferred or released. He grew up in the area and has returned to sell his parents' home. Rose is adamant that she did not kill her baby and tells her story to Stephen using the pages of a Bible on which she has written and drawn an account of her life before her incarceration.
Around 1940, Rose (Rooney Mara), an orphaned young woman, evacuates from Northern Ireland to live with her aunt in the Irish Free State, now known as the Republic of Ireland. There, without any intent, she attracts the interest of many of the local men. She has a brief flirtation with Michael McNulty (Jack Reynor), a Protestant who sympathises with the British war effort and soon leaves to join the RAF. She tries to avoid the inappropriate attention of the local Catholic priest, Father Gaunt (Theo James). She dances with Jack Conroy (Aidan Turner), one of a group of anti-British Catholics. Seeking to avoid trouble after a fight between Father Gaunt and Jack, her aunt sends Rose to live in a deserted farmhouse outside the village.
One day a plane crashes nearby and Rose discovers the pilot hanging from a tree, trapped in his parachute. She cuts him down, discovers it is Michael and shelters him while he recovers, hiding him from the anti-British locals. They grow close and just as he is about to leave they confess their love, have sex, and are quickly married by the local Protestant minister. Before Michael can leave, the anti-British locals seize him from Rose's cottage and later kill him.
Father Gaunt, knowing that Rose had slept with Michael, writes a damning report of Rose's mental health, stating she suffers from "nymphomania". With the permission of her aunt, her only living relative, she is incarcerated in a local mental hospital and there subjected to both insulin shock therapy (insulin coma therapy) and later, electric shock therapy (ECT or electroconvulsive therapy). She discovers that she is pregnant and learns that babies born to single women are given up for adoption or spend their entire lives within the institution. She escapes to the beach. Pursued by Father Gaunt, she swims to a cove where she gives birth. The officer from the Garda Síochána in pursuit in a boat with Gaunt can see Rose striking the ground with a rock and believes that she is killing her newborn son. She was actually severing the umbilical cord with the rock, but Father Gaunt lets the authorities think she is a murderess and takes the baby.

Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 is a 2017 American superhero film directed by James Gunn and produced by Marvel Studios. The movie follows the story of Peter Quill, also known as Star-Lord, who is still trying to find his place among the Guardians of the Galaxy.

Overall, Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 is a visually stunning and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, family, and belonging. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and heartfelt moments, it's no wonder why this movie has become a fan favorite among Marvel enthusiasts.

plot:
Doctor Strange is a 2016 American superhero film directed by Scott Derrickson and produced by Marvel Studios. The movie follows the story of Dr. Stephen Strange, a brilliant but arrogant neurosurgeon who loses the use of his hands in a car accident.

The film begins with Dr. Strange (played by Benedict Cumberbatch), a renowned surgeon at New York Hospital, performing a complex operation to save the life of a young woman. However, during the surgery, he suffers a severe injury that leaves him unable to perform even simple tasks without assistance. Desperate for a solution, Strange travels to Kathmandu in search of a mystical healer known as the Ancient One (played by Tilda Swinton).

The Ancient One is revealed to be a powerful sorceress who has been training a select few in the mystic arts. She recognizes Strange's potential and agrees to teach him the ways of magic, but only if he can demonstrate his commitment to the craft. Strange accepts the challenge and embarks on a journey of self-discovery, learning the fundamentals of magic and facing various challenges along the way.

As Strange delves deeper into the world of magic, he discovers that there is a dark force known as Dormammu (played by Michael Stuhlbarg) that threatens to destroy the universe. The Ancient One reveals that Strange's hands were damaged because they were not worthy of wielding magical energy, but with his newfound abilities, he can now perform complex spells and incantations.

Strange soon finds himself facing off against Dormammu in a battle to save the Earth from destruction. With the help of the Ancient One and other magical beings, including Mordo (played by Chiwetel Ejiofor) and Wong (played by Benedict Wong), Strange must master his newfound powers and confront his own ego in order to defeat Dormammu.

Throughout the film, Strange's character undergoes significant development as he learns to let go of his arrogance and humility. He also forms a bond with Mordo, who becomes a complex and conflicted ally. The film features stunning visual effects, showcasing the magical world that Strange inhabits, including the mystical realm of Kamar-Taj.

The climax of the film takes place in the Dark Dimension, where Strange faces off against Dormammu in an epic battle. With the help of his newfound allies, Strange is able to harness the power of the Eye of Agamotto and defeat Dormammu, saving the universe from destruction.

In the end, Strange returns to New York as a changed man, having found a new sense of purpose and humility. He becomes the Sorcerer Supreme, tasked with protecting the Earth from magical threats. The film concludes on a hopeful note, setting the stage for future adventures in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

Overall, Doctor Strange is a visually stunning and thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, power, and redemption. Benedict Cumberbatch delivers a standout performance as Dr. Strange, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The film's visual effects are breathtaking, transporting audiences to a magical world that is both fantastical and grounded in reality.

Thor is forced to live on a small planet called Sakaar, where he becomes a gladiator and fights in the arena against various alien warriors.

Thor soon discovers that he must stop Hela from unleashing a catastrophic event known as Ragnarok, which will destroy Asgard. He also learns that his hammer Mjolnir has been stolen by Surtur (Clancy Brown), the leader of the Frost Giants.

Along the way, Thor confronts his own identity and purpose, as he struggles to come to terms with being a god and a warrior. He also learns to let go of his ego and trust others, particularly Valkyrie, who becomes a valuable ally in his quest.

The movie features stunning visuals, witty humor, and impressive action sequences, making it a standout in the MCU. The film's tone is lighter and more humorous than previous Thor movies, with Waititi bringing his signature irreverence and wit to the story.

As the battle between Thor and Hela reaches its climax, the fate of Asgard hangs in the balance. In the end, Thor emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. He also learns that he is worthy of wielding Mjolnir once again and becomes a true hero.

The movie concludes with Thor returning to Asgard, where he is welcomed back as a hero. The film ends on a hopeful note, setting the stage for future adventures in the MCU.

Overall, Thor: Ragnarok is a thrilling and entertaining ride that explores themes of identity, purpose, and redemption. With its stunning visuals, witty humor, and impressive action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the MCU and superhero movies in general.

Throughout the film, T'Challa grapples with the weight of his responsibilities as king and the legacy of his father, who was killed in battle against Killmonger. He must also confront his own identity and the expectations placed upon him by his people.

One of the standout aspects of Black Panther is its exploration of themes such as colonialism, imperialism, and cultural identity. The film offers a nuanced portrayal of Wakandan society and culture, highlighting both its strengths and weaknesses. It also features a diverse cast of characters, including Nakia (played by Lupita Nyong'o), a Wakandan spy who becomes T'Challa's love interest.

Overall, Black Panther is a visually stunning and thought-provoking film that offers a fresh take on the superhero genre. Its blend of action, drama, and social commentary makes it a compelling watch for audiences of all ages.

title: Beyond the Reach
overview: A high-rolling corporate shark and his impoverished young guide play the most dangerous game during a hunting trip in the Mojave Desert.
plot:
Ruthless tycoon and trophy collector John Madec flaunts his $500,000 all-terrain vehicle in a small Mojave desert town, buying off the local sheriff to bag an endangered desert bighorn sheep. The sheriff solicits the young but experienced tracker Ben to guide Madec an hour outside of town into the canyon country of Shiprock. Madec taunts Ben over his girlfriend Laina, who has gone away to Colorado on a college swimming scholarship after being gifted a gun that Ben taught her to shoot. When Ben asks to see the permit to hunt the endangered bighorn, Madec offers a wad of cash, which the stunned Ben begrudgingly accepts.
When Madec—with a shoot-first-and-ask-questions-later philosophy—accidentally shoots Charlie, an old prospector, Ben insists that they must report it as an accident. Madec puts another bullet from Ben's gun into the corpse, and after explaining how he can now blackmail Ben with questions of who was the actual killer, offers Ben a deal: Madec will put him through college with a finance major and give him a $300,000-a-year job in return for his complicity in covering up the crime.
When Ben picks up his emergency transponder, Madec destroys it and berates Ben for breaking the deal. Madec then threatens Ben with his high-powered rifle and orders him to strip off his clothes and shoes, forcing him to wander out in the desert, 45 miles from the nearest town, to die of dehydration and exposure. Madec plans to report that Ben went mad, shot Charlie, and wandered off into the barren horizon alone. To ensure his story is not contradicted, Madec watches Ben from a distance, using the scope from his rifle. Ben hides in Charlie's subterranean lair, but Madec blows it up with Charlie's dynamite stash. Before it explodes, Ben escapes with a "treasure map" belonging to Charlie, who Ben vows will not die without justice. Ben finds enough water inside of a barrel to survive. Madec shoots the barrel.
By sunset, Ben uses the map to find a wrist-brace slingshot and some marbles amongst a buried box of Charlie's personal effects. Ben heads for a hidden grotto of water that he and Laina had swum in, only to find it dried up as his sun-burnt body now freezes in the desert night. Madec keeps watch with his vehicle's high-powered floodlights. Ben eventually outsmarts Madec to overcome him with the slingshot.
Back in town, Madec escapes from police custody during a bathroom break to board a helicopter that he solicited using his one phone call. Ben goes to Laina and promises not to leave her side again. An armed Madec sneaks into their house as they sleep and confronts them, but Laina shoots Madec using the same gun Ben gave to her. Madec is then killed by Ben.

title: Top Five
overview: A comedian tries to make it as a serious actor when his reality-TV star fiancé talks him into broadcasting their wedding on her TV show.
plot:
Top Five is a 2014 American romantic comedy-drama written and directed by Chris Rock, who also stars, and produced by Scott Rudin and Eli Bush. Rosario Dawson and Gabrielle Union co-star, with an ensemble of comedians and actors including J. B. Smoove, Kevin Hart, Sherri Shepherd, Tracy Morgan, Cedric the Entertainer and Jerry Seinfeld. After its premiere at the 2014 Toronto International Film Festival, several studios entered a bidding war for distribution rights, which were won by Paramount Pictures; it was released in the United States on 12 December 2014.

Rock plays Andre Allen, a New York comedian and film star who is famous for a lucrative franchise in which he plays Hammy the Bear, a police officer in a bear costume. Now a recovering alcoholic, he wants to be taken seriously and is promoting Uprize, a historical drama in which he plays the Haitian revolutionary Dutty Boukman. He is also preparing for a televised wedding to his fiancée Erica Long, a reality television star played by Union. Chelsea Brown, a New York Times journalist played by Dawson, spends a day following Andre around the city to write a profile of him, even though he is wary of the newspaper, whose critic has repeatedly savaged his work.

As they travel through Manhattan, their conversation ranges over fame, race, comedy, sobriety and relationships. Andre recalls the lowest point of his life, a chaotic night in Houston years earlier that ended with his arrest and set him on the path to recovery. When their limousine is involved in an accident, the pair continue on foot, visiting his old friends and family in the neighbourhood where he grew up, and the friends debate their personal "top five" rappers of all time. Chelsea, who has secrets of her own, gradually breaks down Andre's defences, and the two begin to develop feelings for each other, forcing Andre to question both his upcoming marriage and the direction of his career.

The film draws on Rock's own experiences as a comedian and celebrity and combines sharp stand-up style humour with a reflective look at fame and authenticity.

Top Five received critical acclaim. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 85 percent, with the consensus calling it as smart, funny and trenchant as Rock's best stand-up work and a career highlight for him.

title: Goodnight Mommy
tagline: A mother should look out for her sons.
overview: In the heat of the summer lays a lonesome house in the countryside where nine year old twin brothers await their mother’s return.  When she comes home, bandaged after cosmetic surgery, nothing is like before and the children start to doubt whether this woman is actually who she says she is.
plot:
After undergoing cosmetic facial surgery, a mother returns home to her modern, isolated lakeside house with her ten-year-old twin sons, Elias and Lukas. Her head is covered in bandages, with only her eyes and mouth visible. The twins are unnerved by their mother's appearance and are further taken aback when she begins to exhibit strange behavior. She pointedly ignores Lukas and appears to only acknowledge Elias in conversation. Though it is the middle of summer, the mother orders the twins to keep the blinds closed during the day, imposes a strict rule of silence inside the house, and only permits them to play outdoors. The mother also acts cruel and lashes out at Elias physically when he displays mischievous or disobedient acts, something the boys comment that their mother would never do.
The twins begin to suspect that the woman beneath the bandages is not their real mother. These doubts are confirmed when they find an old photograph of the mother with another unknown woman wearing identical clothes and bearing similar physical traits. Suspicious that the woman residing in their house is an impostor, the twins tie the woman to the bed and torture her to make her confess, sealing her mouth with tape to prevent her from screaming for help.
In the meantime, two employees of the Red Cross appear to collect donations. Although they initially await the return of the mother, they finally leave after Elias discreetly steals a large amount of cash from his mother's purse and offers it to them. Meanwhile, the woman removes the tape and calls for help, but is too late to attract the employees' attention. The twins seal her lips with super glue, but cut them back open with scissors when they realize she is unable to eat.
After she urinates in the bed, the twins briefly free the woman to let her use the restroom, allowing her to subdue them and escape. The twins, however, have set up a booby trap that knocks her unconscious. The woman awakens glued to the living room floor. Elias starts to set fire to the house to pressure her into telling them the truth, but she firmly insists that she is their real mother.
The mother then reveals that Lukas is dead, having died in an accident prior to the events of the movie; Elias has been hallucinating his presence. She tearfully insists to Elias that Lukas's death was not his fault and begs him to free her so they can both move on from the tragedy. Elias asks her what Lukas is doing, but she, unable to see the apparition of Lukas threatening to set fire to a curtain, cannot answer. Elias, believing his real mother would be able to see Lukas, grabs his arm and lights up the curtain. The mother burns to death before the firefighters arrive. The film ends with a ghostly shot of the mother reunited with her sons at a cornfield near their home.

title: Testament of Youth
tagline: Divided by war. United by love.
overview: Testament of Youth is a powerful story of love, war and remembrance, based on the First World War memoir by Vera Brittain, which has become the classic testimony of that war from a woman’s point of view. A searing journey from youthful hopes and dreams to the edge of despair and back again, it’s a film about young love, the futility of war and how to make sense of the darkest times.
plot:
In 1914, Vera Brittain wants to escape her traditional family in Buxton by attending Oxford University with her younger brother Edward and his friends at Uppingham School, Roland Leighton and Victor Richardson. Despite her father's opposition, she passes the entrance examination for Somerville College, Oxford. Before enrolling at Oxford, Vera and Roland, who shares Vera's interest in writing and poetry, begin a romance, although she knows that Victor is in love with her.
After the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand and the start of the First World War, Vera helps to persuade her father to allow Edward to join the army instead of studying at Oxford; Roland and Victor also join, and Roland is the first to reach the Western Front. As long lists of casualties appear in newspapers, Vera leaves Oxford to volunteer for the Voluntary Aid Detachment as a nurse tending the wounded in a hospital in England.
Although his friends still see the war as exciting, Roland tells Vera of his traumatic experiences from trench warfare at the front. He proposes to Vera; they decide to marry during his next home leave. Roland returns to France, now with Edward. Roland writes in late 1915 that he has been granted leave and is safe away from the front. As Vera awaits his arrival during the Christmas holiday, Roland's mother tells her on the telephone that he has been killed.
The army tells Vera and Roland's family that he died "a noble and painless death." After she demands the truth, George Catlin, who saw the wounded Roland in Louvencourt, admits that Roland died in agonising pain from his abdominal gunshot wound. When Victor, blind from his injuries, arrives at Vera's hospital, she proposes to him because he is "going to need someone and I... well, Roland would like it," but he gently turns her down before suddenly dying from his head injury.
In 1917, Vera asks to transfer to France to be closer to Edward, but her first assignment is to treat wounded Germans. She is reluctant, but learns that they suffer and die like English soldiers. Vera finds Edward among the dying and helps save his life. He shows her a letter from his "dear friend" Geoffrey Thurlow, implying the two men were lovers. After Edward's recovery, she is glad that he is sent to the safer Italian Front. Edward insists that Vera return to her Oxford studies after the war. Vera returns home after her mother has a nervous breakdown. She sees a telegram being delivered and learns, from her father's weeping, that Edward has died.
In 1918, having lost all the young men closest to her, Vera cannot celebrate as crowds cheer the Armistice with Germany. Back at Oxford, she has nightmares about Roland's and Edward's deaths. Winifred Holtby, another student at the college, helps Vera cope with her trauma.
Vera attends a public meeting where speakers debate how to punish Germany for the war.
